writes.detail: The running slot yields. updateScriptPtr saves the resume offset in vm.slot[].offs, and _currentScript=0xFF ends the executeScript loop. The slot stays ssRunning, so nothing about it changes from a script's point of view.

blocks.until: Until the next runAllScripts pass reaches this slot, which is in the next main-loop iteration. didexec is set on every opcode, so the slot is not re-run in the same pass. Only this slot yields. If the slot was started nested (startScript-style calls, or an engine hook through runScriptNested), control goes back to the caller, which carries on in the same frame if it is still alive and not frozen. A slot frozen in the meantime (status|=0x80) is skipped until it is unfrozen. In v5 no script code runs earlier in an iteration than runAllScripts. processInput's only script-related action is abortCutscene on Esc, which moves an override slot's offset but executes nothing. The pre/post save-load scripts in handleSaveLoad are v6 only. So a yield always resumes in a later iteration.
blocks.cite: script.cpp:506-507; script.cpp:968-985; script.cpp:344-388; script.cpp:914-930; scumm.cpp:3214; scumm.cpp:3231-3232; input.cpp:1423-1424; scumm.cpp:3418-3419

cost_knobs.effect: Sets the frame length in jiffies. A value <1 is forced to 1. The main loop waits delta*4 quarter-frames before the next scummLoop, so one breakHere costs VAR_TIMER_NEXT jiffies of game time. At the start of that scummLoop, VAR_TIMER is set to delta, VAR_TIMER_TOTAL and VAR_TMR_1..3 increase by delta, paused slots' delays drop by min(delta,15), and _talkDelay drops by delta.
Converts quarter-frames to milliseconds (wall-clock only). It is 240 Hz for MI1.

These only shorten the sleep: the per-frame delay becomes 0 ms (10 ms under Ctrl-F). VAR_TIMER and the other per-frame counters do not change. Under the project's speedrun bridge, onWait still counts the delta*4 quarter-frames on the run clock and advances the CD music timer once per quarter-frame, so VAR_MUSIC_TIMER (copied every loop) gains about delta per frame whatever skipWaits says. In stock ScummVM the CD timer runs on a wall-clock thread, so fast mode makes VAR_MUSIC_TIMER advance less per frame.
cost_knobs.cite: scumm.cpp:2919-2927; input.cpp:150-153; speedrun/speedrun_bridge.cpp:415-432; soundcd.cpp:108-127; scumm.cpp:3200; sound.cpp:2219-2221

cost_knobs.effect: A frozen slot is not resumed by runAllScripts, so the wait gets longer.

Esc works only while VAR_CUTSCENEEXIT_KEY is nonzero. If this slot holds a pending override, Esc moves its offset to the override target, sets it ssRunning, clears freezeCount and sets VAR_OVERRIDE=1. That happens in processInput, before runAllScripts in the same iteration, so the resume point changes and the rest of the breakHere loop is skipped.

game_specific: GID_LOOM PC-Engine English, one script slot in one room: breakHere also pauses that slot for 120 jiffies (delay=120, status=ssPaused) to imitate a loading screen. It does not apply to MI1 (script_v5.cpp:825-828).

Frame-length guards in the main loop for other games: v0 DelayCalculateDelta (scumm.cpp:2845), Maniac v1 non-NES rounds up to a multiple of 3 (scumm.cpp:2853), kEnhUIUX save-name rooms in Indy3/Loom/Zak (scumm.cpp:2862), COMI menu room (scumm.cpp:2880). None applies to MI1 DOS CD.
rows.notes: This is the basic per-frame yield (4625 lines in MI1). In v5 each scummLoop runs in this order: processInput, handleSaveLoad, runAllScripts, checkExecVerbs, checkAndRunSentenceScript, then walkActors, moveCamera, drawing, actors and effects (scumm.cpp:3177, 3214, 3231-3232, 3255, 3284-3296). VAR_MAIN_SCRIPT is mapped only for HE99+ (vars.cpp:359), so its call (scumm.cpp:3298-3299) never runs in v5. A slot that yields in runAllScripts, checkExecVerbs or the sentence script sees exactly one walkActors/moveCamera step before it resumes. A slot that yields inside the scroll script sees none. moveCamera starts that script through VAR_SCROLL_SCRIPT after walkActors (camera.cpp:162-165), and MI1 sets that var. runAllScripts clears didexec at its start (script.cpp:971-972), but in v5 nothing runs script code before it in an iteration, so a slot cannot resume in the iteration it yielded in.

writes.detail: The result variable becomes its current value + 1. It can be a global _scummVars entry, a bit variable (0x8000, stored in _bitVars in v5), or a local of the current slot (0x4000). With 0x2000 it is indexed by a following word or var. There is no clamp (int32 storage). For a bit variable the bit always becomes 1, because value+1 is nonzero.

Side effects when the target is an engine var that writeVar handles specially. VAR_NOSUBTITLES (v5): the 'subtitles' setting becomes !value. readVar returns !subtitles for that var, so increment writes 1 (subtitles were on and turn off) or 2, and 2 fails assert(value==0||value==1). VAR_CHARINC: in room 0 with a target 'talkspeed' setting, the written value is replaced by 9-getTalkSpeed(), so the user setting wins over current+1. Otherwise a value of 0..9 is saved as the user talk speed 9-value, which is the text-speed setting.

game_specific: writeVar guards for other games: GID_SAMNMAX rewrites VAR_TIMER_NEXT in one script (script.cpp:766), and GID_LOOM v<4 sets the fire animation speed on VAR_TIMER_NEXT (script.cpp:786). readVar guards: GID_MONKEY2 remaps a copy-protection var (script.cpp:584), and GID_MONKEY2 Mac forces VAR_MACHINE_SPEED (script.cpp:599). None applies to MI1.
v<=3 (except Indy3 FM-Towns and Loom PCE) packs bit variables into _scummVars (script.cpp:811-821). v5 uses _bitVars (script.cpp:822-830).
GF_FEW_LOCALS masks the local index to 0xF (script.cpp:835-839).
rows.notes: MI1 forms: Var 651, Local 181. Most engine VAR_ slots are plain storage, so incrementing one acts like setting it, and whatever engine path reads that var sees the new value. Some are overwritten by the engine every loop, so an increment there does not last: VAR_TIMER is reset to delta at loop start (scumm.cpp:3110-3111), and scummLoop_updateScummVars rewrites VAR_CAMERA_POS_X, VAR_HAVE_MSG, VAR_VIRT_MOUSE_X/Y, VAR_MOUSE_X/Y and VAR_DEBUGMODE (scumm.cpp:3378-3392). A local is readable only by the same slot.

reads: var (global, bit or local via readVar, including the 0x2000 indexed form)
operand: signed word constant or var
game_specific: readVar guards (GID_MONKEY2 copy-protection remap and Mac VAR_MACHINE_SPEED, HE online mods) do not apply to MI1 (script.cpp:583-616).
In v5, VAR_NOSUBTITLES reads return !ConfMan 'subtitles' rather than the stored value (script.cpp:592-593; vars.cpp:173-175).
rows.notes: a=var and b=operand, both truncated to int16. jumpRelative(b<a) falls through when var > operand and otherwise adds the offset (script_v5.cpp:402-409, 1636-1640). descumm prints it as 'unless (Var > N) goto'. It is a pure test and changes only the script pointer. In MI1 it also tests vars the engine rewrites every loop in scummLoop_updateScummVars: VAR_MOUSE_X/Y, VAR_VIRT_MOUSE_Y, VAR_CAMERA_POS_X and VAR_DEBUGMODE (scumm.cpp:3378-3392). VAR_MACHINE_SPEED, which MI1 also tests, is not written by the v5 engine; its only engine writes are for v2 Zak and HE (vars.cpp:608, 682, 809). VAR_CURSORSTATE is written by the cursorCommand opcode (script_v5.cpp:935), not by the main loop.

writes.detail: VAR_CAMERA_MIN_X and VAR_CAMERA_MAX_X are set from the two operands, each clamped to [_screenWidth/2, _roomWidth-_screenWidth/2].

cost_knobs.knob: new bounds vs current camera position
cost_knobs.effect: If the camera now lies outside [MIN,MAX], each later moveCamera call steps it 8 px toward the bound and returns early, with no actor follow or pan that frame. The correction therefore takes several frames. Under VAR_CAMERA_FAST_X or _snapScroll it snaps at once. Narrower bounds also shorten later pans and follows, because their target is clamped.

game_specific: paramsBeforeOpcode applies only to v3 non-PCE, so v5 reads operands after the sub-opcode (script_v5.cpp:2352, 2362-2365).
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_SCROLL. The engine clamps the camera to these bounds in setCameraAt and moveCamera (camera.cpp:46-50, 101-112, 141-145), so they change VAR_CAMERA_POS_X (scumm.cpp:3379) and how far, and so how long, later camera pans and follows travel. Every room entry overwrites both vars with defaults (room.cpp:202-205), so the effect lasts until the next room load.

game_specific: GF_SMALL_HEADER (set only by the ScummEngine_v4 constructor, so v3/v4) sets _roomPalette[b]=a and _fullRedraw. In v5 the else branch calls error('room-color is no longer a valid command'), which stops the engine (script_v5.cpp:2378-2387; scumm.cpp:576-578; detection_tables.h:199).
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_COLOR. It has no valid effect in v5 because MI1 DOS CD is v5 without GF_SMALL_HEADER.

writes.detail: initScreens(b,h) frees the rtBuffer resources and rebuilds the virtual screens: text [0,b), main room [b,h) and verb [h,screenHeight). It also sets _screenB and _screenH and reinitialises gdi.
read_back_by: engine VAR_VIRT_MOUSE_X/VAR_VIRT_MOUSE_Y (computed against the main virtscreen top and height), testable with o5_isEqual/o5_isLess/o5_isLessEqual etc.
click area code passed to the input script (scene vs verb area) by checkExecVerbs

game_specific: FM-Towns: initScreens clears layers, and for games other than GID_MONKEY also clears the text surface (gfx.cpp:350-360). Not DOS.
NES adds a 16-pixel shift, v7+ uses a different banner, and the Mac screen is cleared (gfx.cpp:362-385). None applies to MI1 DOS CD.
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_SCREEN. MI1 uses only two layouts (main from 0 to 144 with verbs below, or full height to 200). This is not purely visual. It moves the boundary that decides whether a click is a scene click or a verb-area click (verbs.cpp:689), and the range in which VAR_VIRT_MOUSE_Y is valid rather than -1 (input.cpp:431-434). The main screen height also sets the cell count of a later DOS dissolve fade (40 x height/4), and so how many RNG draws and waits it takes (gfx.cpp:4640-4641, 4687, 4764). See screenEffect.

writes.detail: setPalColor(index, r, g, b) writes _currentPalette[index] and marks that colour dirty. Under EGA render mode it updates _egaColorMap instead.

reads: operands r,g,b (word or var) and index (byte or var)
game_specific: GID_MONKEY (all v5 MI1 releases including DOS CD): in the Captain Smirk close-up room, SetPalColor for palette index 3 is skipped when kEnhVisualChanges is enabled (script_v5.cpp:2427-2434).
The GF_SMALL_HEADER branch (v3/v4 only) instead writes _shadowPalette[b]=a (script_v5.cpp:2400-2414).
setPalColor: heversion 70 index remap and GID_INDY4 Amiga palette mapping (palette.cpp:1414-1415, 1426-1459). Not MI1.
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_PALETTE, large-header form. No v5 opcode reads the palette back. The room palette is reloaded on room entry, so the change lasts until the next palette load. The EGA render-mode path (palette.cpp:1405-1411) is chosen by a user setting, not by game id.

writes.detail: setShake(1): _shakeEnabled=true, _shakeFrame=0, shake position reset, and a full redraw if the setting changed. The shake is animated in waitForTimer.

rows.notes: SO_ROOM_SHAKE_ON. Visual only, and no opcode can read it back. Scripts time the shake with breakHere or delay loops.

writes.detail: setShake(0): _shakeEnabled=false, _shakeFrame=0, shake position reset, and a full redraw if the setting changed.

rows.notes: SO_ROOM_SHAKE_OFF. Visual only.

writes.detail: setScaleSlot(e-1, 0, b, a, 0, d, c) sets scale slot endpoints y1=b, scale1=a, y2=d, scale2=c (x1=x2=0). Boxes whose scale field has 0x8000 take their scale from that slot.
read_back_by: o5_getActorScale (indirect: reads actor _scalex after setupActorScale recomputes it from a box that references this slot)

rows.notes: SO_ROOM_SCALE. setScaleSlot asserts 1<=slot (boxes.cpp:436), so e must be >= 2. The third sub-opcode byte's value is read through PARAM_2, which matches descumm's comment. _scaleSlots is saved in savegames (saveload.cpp:1772). Unused in MI1.

writes.detail: darkenPalette(a,a,a,start,end) sets _currentPalette[start..end] to the room palette scaled by a/255, capped at 252 in v5-6, and marks the colours dirty.

game_specific: darkenPalette: GID_INDY4 Amiga path (palette.cpp:1053-1103), EGA-dithering path (palette.cpp:1104-1140), and the max=252 clamp for v5-6 non-HE (palette.cpp:1143-1148).
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_INTENSITY. Visual only, with no read-back. Scripts fade by calling it repeatedly with breakHere in between, so any time cost comes from those breakHere calls.

writes.detail: Queues a save or load: _saveLoadFlag=operand1 (0 = nothing happens, 1 = save, any other nonzero value = load), _saveLoadSlot forced to 99, _saveTemporaryState=true. A load later replaces the whole game state from that slot.

When the queued operation runs, VAR_GAME_LOADED becomes GAME_PROPER_SAVE (201) after a successful temporary save, or GAME_PROPER_LOAD (203) after a successful temporary load. With the original GUI, failure codes (202/204) are written instead.

blocks.until: The script does not yield. It runs on to its next yield in the same pass. A load queued in runAllScripts, checkExecVerbs or the sentence script runs later in the same frame, through 'goto load_game' after checkAndRunSentenceScript. A load queued after that point (for example in the scroll script that moveCamera starts) waits for the next frame's handleSaveLoad. A save always runs in the next frame's handleSaveLoad, before runAllScripts.

game_specific: v6 only: pre and post save/load scripts run around it (scumm.cpp:3418-3419, 3448-3449). v8 only: VAR_GAME_LOADED cleared first (scumm.cpp:3414-3415).
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_SAVEGAME. The operand2 slot is overwritten with 99 (script_v5.cpp:2461-2462). Unused in MI1. A load never interrupts this opcode, because it runs after the issuing script has yielded. Whatever that script does between this opcode and its next yield is therefore thrown away by the load. A save captures the state at the start of the next frame, so it includes those effects.

writes.detail: If a!=0: _switchRoomEffect = low byte (the fade-in used at the next room entry) and _switchRoomEffect2 = high byte (the fade-out at the next startScene). Nothing is shown now. Both persist until set again.
If a==0: fadeIn(_newEffect) runs the stored fade-in at once. It updates the palette, runs the transition, and sets _screenEffectFlag=true.

Deferred RNG consumption. When the scheduled fade-in or fade-out code is 128, dissolveEffectSelector runs dissolveEffect(8,4) on DOS. That shuffles the cell order with _rnd.getRandomNumber once per cell minus one: 40 x mainScreenHeight/4 cells, so 1439 draws at height 144 and 1999 at height 200. Codes 134 and 135 do the same at pixel or column granularity. _rnd is the same RandomSource that o5_getRandomNr draws from, so every later random result shifts. With a!=0 the draws happen at the next room change (fadeOut inside startScene, or fadeIn in scummLoop_handleEffects). With a==0 they happen immediately. MI1's 0x8180 form (fade-in 128) triggers this.

reads: _screenEffectFlag (fadeOut acts only if a fadeIn ran since the previous fadeOut)

blocks.until: The script never yields. With a!=0 (every MI1 use) the opcode returns at once, and the cost is paid at the next room change. fadeOut runs synchronously inside startScene, in the middle of the script that changes the room. fadeIn runs in scummLoop_handleEffects later in the same scummLoop iteration, because startScene sets _doEffect. With a==0 the opcode runs the fade-in synchronously. Either way the waitForTimer loops stall the engine and no scummLoop runs, so VAR_TIMER, script delays and walking do not advance. The CD music timer does advance: VAR_MUSIC_TIMER is copied from it every loop. Under the speedrun bridge, each waited quarter-frame also counts on the run clock.

cost_knobs.knob: effect code (the low or high byte of a)
cost_knobs.effect: 0 = nothing. 1-6 = transitionEffect(code-1): a fixed iteration count from the table, each iteration waiting VAR_FADE_DELAY quarter-frames. 128 = dissolveEffect(8,4) on DOS, with one 1-quarter-frame wait per cell whose offset is below the main screen height (18 waits at height 144). 129 = nothing on fade-in, a black blit on fade-out. 130-133 = scrollEffect on fade-in only, waiting VAR_FADE_DELAY per 8-px step; on fade-out these codes call error(). 134/135 = dissolveEffect(1,1) and dissolveEffect(1,h). Any other code calls error(). fadeOut does nothing unless a fadeIn ran since the previous fadeOut (_screenEffectFlag).
Quarter-frames per transition or scroll iteration.

_fastMode makes transitionEffect skip its waitForTimer call entirely, so those iterations are counted nowhere. skipWaits and _fastMode&2 only zero the sleep inside waitForTimer. The speedrun bridge's onWait still counts the quarter-frames and advances the CD timer. Dissolve and scroll waits have no _fastMode check.
Sets the dissolve cell count (40 x height/4), and so its RNG draws and wait count. It also sets the transitionEffect height.

game_specific: FM-Towns: values 8-13, 16-22 and 30 are layer and palette control commands that return early (script_v5.cpp:2468-2520). Not DOS.
fadeIn/fadeOut are disabled for GID_MANIAC Amiga (gfx.cpp:4384, 4444). The Dig _disableFadeInEffect (gfx.cpp:4384-4395).

transitionEffect: Amiga per-frame timing and the C64 default delay (gfx.cpp:4528-4555). dissolveEffectSelector: Loom v4 / Loom PCE / Mac variants, otherwise dissolveEffect(8,4) (gfx.cpp:4963-4978). dissolveEffect returns at once on Mac screens (gfx.cpp:4625-4626).
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_FADE. MI1 calls it with 0x8181 (in=129, out=129: no transition), 0x8180 (in=128 dissolve, out=129) and 0x0101 (iris in and out). It never calls it with 0, so in MI1 the opcode only sets state that the next room change consumes. After an effect, _lastWaitTime is set to the effect's end (scumm.cpp:2974), so the next frame still waits its full delta on top. scummLoop_handleEffects also calls clearClickedStatus after the scheduled fade-in (scumm.cpp:4124), which drops pending clicks.

writes.detail: darkenPalette(r,g,b,start,end) sets _currentPalette[start..end] to the room palette with separate red, green and blue scale factors (capped at 252 in v5).

reads: operands (word or var for r,g,b; byte or var for start,end)
game_specific: Same darkenPalette guards as RoomIntensity: Indy4 Amiga and the EGA-dither paths (palette.cpp:1053-1140).
rows.notes: SO_RGB_ROOM_INTENSITY. Visual only.

writes.detail: setShadowPalette(r,g,b,start,end,0,256) rebuilds the _shadowPalette remap table for all 256 colours: each colour maps to the nearest room colour in start..end after scaling.

game_specific: GID_INDY4 Amiga: setShadowPalette is a no-op (palette.cpp:969-970).
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_SHADOW. Used for actor shadow rendering. Visual only, and unused in MI1.

writes.detail: Writes string resource a (NUL-terminated) to a save file named after the target, <target>.cfg for GID_MONKEY. The inline filename is ignored.
VAR_SOUNDRESULT=0 if the file opened.

game_specific: GID_INDY4 writes <target>.iq. GID_MONKEY and GID_MONKEY2 write <target>.cfg (meant for the MI fan speech patch). Any other game calls error() (script_v5.cpp:2571-2577).
rows.notes: SO_SAVE_STRING. Not used by the original MI1 DOS CD scripts.

writes.detail: If the <target>.cfg (GID_MONKEY) file exists, its whole contents are loaded into string resource a via loadPtrToResource. Nothing changes if the file is missing.

game_specific: Same filename guard as saveString: GID_INDY4 uses .iq, GID_MONKEY/GID_MONKEY2 use .cfg, anything else errors (script_v5.cpp:2600-2606).
rows.notes: SO_LOAD_STRING. The value kind is player_input because it comes from a file outside the game state. Unused in MI1.

writes.detail: palManipulateInit(res, start, end, time) takes target RGB from string resources res, res+1 and res+2 and sets _palManipCounter=time. Each frame after that, palManipulate moves _currentPalette[start..end) toward the target.

cost_knobs.effect: Number of frames the palette transition runs (one palManipulate step per scummLoop). The script does not wait for it.

game_specific: FM-Towns ignores it unless _townsPaletteFlags&1. GID_INDY4 Amiga and EGA dithering make it a no-op (palette.cpp:823-835).
rows.notes: SO_ROOM_TRANSFORM. Visual only, and unused in MI1. It calls error() if a string resource is missing (palette.cpp:840-844).

writes.detail: _colorCycle[a-1].delay = 0x4000/(b*0x4C), or 0 when b=0. This is the speed of palette cycle a.

rows.notes: SO_CYCLE_SPEED. Asserts 1<=a<=16 (script_v5.cpp:2637). Visual only, and unused in MI1. Any other sub-opcode calls error() (script_v5.cpp:2640-2642).

reads: var (word index read with fetchScriptWord, then readVar: global, bit or local, including the indexed form)
operand: signed word constant or var
game_specific: GID_INDY3 FM-Towns, two script slots in one room, operand -256, with kEnhGameBreakingBugFixes: the test is replaced by an unconditional jump (biplane controls fix) (script_v5.cpp:1653-1658).
GID_LOOM v>=4 English, one script slot, VAR_MUSIC_TIMER compared with 1708, with kEnhVisualChanges: the operand becomes 1815 (distaff note timing) (script_v5.cpp:1666-1668).
Neither applies to MI1. The readVar guards are as for o5_isLess.
rows.notes: a=var (int16) and b=operand. jumpRelative(b<=a) falls through when var >= operand and otherwise jumps (script_v5.cpp:1670; 402-409). descumm prints it as 'if (X >= N)' / 'unless (X >= N)'. It is a pure test.

writes.detail: The result var gets the Chebyshev distance max(|dx|,|dy|) between two objects or actors (getObjActToObjActDist). It is 0 if both are actors in the same nonzero room that is not the current room. It is 0xFF if either side cannot be placed in the current room.

reads: object_owner and inventory (whereIsObject; an object in inventory takes its actor owner's position if that actor is in the current room)
object walk point (walk_x/walk_y of the room object, not its hotspot)

walk_boxes (only when the first operand is an actor and the second an object: the object's point is first snapped into the actor's nearest walk box, using box flags kBoxInvisible/kBoxPlayerOnly and actor _ignoreBoxes)
game_specific: _game.version==0: both operands are actor ids and are converted with actorToObj (script_v5.cpp:1415-1418). Not MI1.

adjustXYToBeInBox: GF_SMALL_HEADER sets the first valid box to 0 (actor.cpp:1990), and v<=4 falls back to the last valid XY (actor.cpp:2012-2014). In v5 the box search starts at 1 and the fallback is the original point.
rows.notes: Ids below _numActors (13 in v5) are treated as actors (object.cpp:1620-1622; scumm.cpp:1739-1740); higher ids are objects. Every actor slot 0..12, including 0, is valid, because isValidActor only checks _number == id (actor.cpp:2277-2279, 107-108; scumm.cpp:2088-2101). So only a negative id makes derefActorSafe return null and gives 0xFF. Id 0 gives 0xFF only because actor 0 normally stays in room 0 (actor.cpp:185-187; actor.h:267-269). An object gives 0xFF when it is <1 or >= _numGlobalObjects, when it is not in the current room, or when it is owned but not in _inventory (object.cpp:351-379). Box snapping is asymmetric, so getDist(actor, object) can differ from getDist(object, actor) (object.cpp:546-550). adjustXYToBeInBox also writes the actor's _lastValidX/Y scratch fields (actor.cpp:2052-2053, 2065-2066), but only v<=4 reads them (actor.cpp:2014), so it has no effect in v5. Opcode bits select which operands are vars (descumm shows forms with VAR_EGO and constants).

writes.detail: For each following byte j >= 0x80 until 0: _resourceMapper[j&0x7F] = i (the real room resource). Bytes below 0x80 are ignored.
read_back_by: engine VAR_ROOM_RESOURCE (set to the mapped resource when a room numbered >= 0x80 is loaded), testable with o5_isEqual etc.

game_specific: Mapping is used only when version<7 and heversion<=71 (room.cpp:166; resource.cpp:604-606).
rows.notes: No opcode reads _resourceMapper directly. Its consumers are startScene (VAR_ROOM keeps the pseudo number >= 0x80, while _roomResource and VAR_ROOM_RESOURCE get the mapped room; room.cpp:155, 166-171), ensureResourceLoaded (resource.cpp:604-606) and resourceRoutines load/lock/unlock room (script_v5.cpp:2250, 2283, 2303). So one room resource can appear as several room numbers, each with its own VAR_ROOM value. It is saved in savegames (saveload.cpp:1425). MI1 sets its mappings from a global script. descumm prints each mapped byte as j&127 and 'IG' for ignored bytes; that is tools code, not engine code (third_party/scummvm-tools/engines/scumm/descumm.cpp:1044-1061).

writes.detail: The result var gets the id in [VAR_ACTOR_RANGE_MIN, VAR_ACTOR_RANGE_MAX] with the smallest getObjActToObjActDist to the operand, or 0xFF if none is closer than 255.

game_specific: The same helper guards as o5_getDist. The v2 table also uses this opcode, with v2's own VAR_ACTOR_RANGE_MIN/MAX indices (script_v2.cpp:168, 328; vars.cpp:141-142). v5 maps them to engine slots (vars.cpp:51-52).
rows.notes: No engine code writes VAR_ACTOR_RANGE_MIN/MAX, so scripts must set them. The scan counts down from MAX and keeps an id only if it is strictly closer, so on a tie the higher id wins. It does not skip the operand itself: if the operand is in range and placeable, its own distance is 0 and it returns itself. The do-while runs at least once even when MAX < MIN. Distances of 255 or more, and unplaceable ids (0xFF), are never chosen. Despite the name, ids in the range at or above _numActors (13 in v5) are scanned as objects, and id 0 as actor 0, with the same rules as o5_getDist (object.cpp:1620-1622). When the operand is an actor, object candidates are box-snapped (object.cpp:546-550). Unused in MI1 (0 lines).

writes.detail: Global variable _scummVars[n] = operand. The target can be indexed: with the 0x2000 flag, getResultPos adds a constant or another variable's value.
Bit variable (target has the 0x8000 flag): the _bitVars bit is set if the value is nonzero and cleared if it is zero (v4+ layout).
Local variable vm.localvar[current slot][n] (target has the 0x4000 flag). Only the same script slot can read it back, and it dies with that slot, so it cannot gate logic across scripts.

Writing VAR_NOSUBTITLES (var 60 in v5) also sets the ScummVM config 'subtitles' = !value (asserts that the value is 0 or 1). Later reads of VAR_NOSUBTITLES return !config 'subtitles', not _scummVars, so the user's options dialog can change what scripts read. VAR_SUBTITLES is 0xFF (unused) in v5.

Writing VAR_CHARINC sets the talk speed (setTalkSpeed(9 - value)) when the value is 0..9. In room 0, if the target has a 'talkspeed' config key, the user's setting replaces the script value. VAR_CHARINC is the per-character message delay. This side effect is in writeVar, so every opcode that stores through setResult has it. MI1 sets VAR_CHARINC with o5_expression, not o5_move.

Engine hook variables choose which scripts the engine starts later: VAR_ENTRY_SCRIPT and VAR_ENTRY_SCRIPT2 (runEntryScript, before and after the room's own entry code), VAR_EXIT_SCRIPT and VAR_EXIT_SCRIPT2 (runExitScript, before and after the room's own exit code), VAR_VERB_SCRIPT (runInputScript), VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT (checkAndRunSentenceScript), VAR_INVENTORY_SCRIPT (runInventoryScript), VAR_CUTSCENE_START_SCRIPT and VAR_CUTSCENE_END_SCRIPT (beginCutscene/endCutscene), VAR_SCROLL_SCRIPT (setCameraAt/moveCamera). MI1 writes VAR_ENTRY_SCRIPT2 with o5_move.

VAR_EGO picks the actor that later engine actions use: o5_pickupObject sets the object's owner to VAR_EGO, o5_loadRoomWithEgo moves the VAR_EGO actor into the new room, and o5_printEgo makes VAR_EGO the speaker. Writing it redirects those later writes. MI1 writes it with o5_move.

Scripts use it to set the engine-observed VARs (hook scripts, special keys, timers, VAR_TIMER_NEXT, VAR_NOSUBTITLES, VAR_EGO). writes.detail: Registers the skip point: vm.cutScenePtr[cutSceneStackPointer] = script offset of the jump right after this op (saved before that jump is skipped); vm.cutSceneScript[...] = current slot. The jump (1 opcode byte + 1 word) is then skipped without being checked.
VAR_OVERRIDE = 0 (only when _game.version >= 5).
Deferred, on Esc: abortCutscene sets VAR_OVERRIDE = 1 if a skip point is registered at the current cutscene level.

Deferred, on Esc: the registered slot gets offs = saved jump, so it executes the jump and skips the override block. Also status = ssRunning and freezeCount = 0, which cancels any pending delay, wait or freeze. cutsceneOverride is decremented and cutScenePtr cleared.

starts.what: Nothing directly. Registers the current slot so that Esc (abortCutscene) later resumes it at the skip jump, even if it is paused or frozen.

cost_knobs.effect: Calls abortCutscene: the overriding script jumps past the rest of the override block, so delays and waits in it cost nothing. abortCutscene does not stop walks, animations or messages already started (its body only redirects the slot and stops TTS). VAR_CUTSCENEEXIT_KEY's value is then copied to _mouseAndKeyboardStat, so when user input is on (_userPut > 0) the same Esc also reaches VAR_VERB_SCRIPT as a key event.

rows.notes: Splits o5_beginOverride on its operand byte: nonzero = beginOverride (script_v5.cpp:2010-2014). It works at cutscene level 0 too; no cutscene is required. Only the innermost level's skip point is used, and a second beginOverride at the same level replaces the first. beginOverride does not increment slot.cutsceneOverride (beginCutscene does, script.cpp:1634), but abortCutscene and endCutscene decrement it (script.cpp:1703-1704, 1654-1655, 1662-1663). The skip point is cleared only by endOverride (script.cpp:1732-1733), endCutscene at that level (1665-1666), abortCutscene (1707), beginCutscene for the new level (1641-1642) and engine reset (scumm.cpp:2124). It is saved in savegames (saveload.cpp:1493-1494). It is keyed by slot index, so nothing clears it when the registering script stops or the room changes. In MI1 every beginOverride is followed by a goto past the skippable block. No opcode can read the skip point itself; scripts see the skip only through VAR_OVERRIDE.

writes.detail: Text-slot parameters (_string[slot]: xpos/ypos, color, right clip, center, overhead). The actor argument picks the slot: 252->3, 253->2, 254->1, anything else->0. The slot is first loaded from its saved defaults. Modifiers (Pos/Color/Clipped/Center/Left/Overhead) change the live values. They become the new defaults (saveDefault) only when the modifier list ends with no Text. With Text, decodeParseString returns before saveDefault, so the changes apply to that one message only. The engine also rewrites live values: on each page, displayDialog recomputes _string[0].xpos/ypos from the speaker for overhead text; drawString leaves _string[1].xpos at the right edge of the drawn text; showMessageDialog sets _string[3].color = 4 when it is 0. No v5 opcode reads these values, and the next print to the slot reloads its defaults. Modifier code 3 (Erase), code 8 (SayVoice, outside Loom) and codes 5 and 9-14 are hard errors.

writes.detail: VAR_HAVE_MSG (slot 0: actor or narrator 255) is set to 0xFF when the message starts. The engine then drives _haveMsg: 1 at end of text, 0xFF again at each embedded wait code (0xFF 0x03), 0 at the keep-text code (0xFF 0x02), and 0 when stopTalk runs. stopTalk runs after the last page's talk delay runs out, on a room change, and when the camera scrolls while the text is on screen (v4-6 redrawBGAreas and setCameraAt call stopTalk when camera._cur.x != camera._last.x and _charset->_hasMask). VAR_HAVE_MSG is re-mirrored from _haveMsg every frame. If the speaking actor is not in the current room, actorTalk returns before this point, so nothing is set and nothing is shown.

blocks.until: Never yields: o5_print returns at once and the message runs out over later frames. Scripts block on it with o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_MESSAGE (until VAR_HAVE_MSG == 0). Exception: actor 252 with a Text opens a modal banner or dialog that stops the whole engine (no scummLoop frames, no jiffies) until a key or click. The Ultimate-Talkie-only branch re-runs print after breakHere; it does not apply to the DOS CD release.

cost_knobs.effect: Adds VAR_CHARINC jiffies to _talkDelay per printed character. Characters count even with subtitles off. The ScummVM talkspeed setting maps to it (VAR_CHARINC = 9 - talkspeed). A script write to VAR_CHARINC also writes the talkspeed config.

cost_knobs.knob: base talk delay (VAR_DEFAULT_TALK_DELAY unset in v5)
cost_knobs.effect: Each message page starts with a fixed 60 jiffies, because v5 does not map VAR_DEFAULT_TALK_DELAY (it stays 0xFF).
Split one print into pages. Each page pays its own base 60 plus per-character delay, and VAR_HAVE_MSG stays nonzero until the last page ends.
_talkDelay counts down by min(VAR_TIMER_NEXT,15) jiffies per scummLoop frame. Wall time is roughly constant, but the number of frames is about delay/min(VAR_TIMER_NEXT,15).
If VAR_TALKSTOP_KEY != 0, pressing '.' sets _talkDelay = 0, so the current page ends on the next displayDialog.
Esc only calls abortCutscene, which jumps the overridden script to its override point and sets VAR_OVERRIDE. It does not clear _talkDelay or the message.

In v4-6, displayDialog does nothing while camera._dest differs from camera._cur, or while camera._cur differs from camera._last. A pending message does not start, and its delay does not run, until the camera stops. A scroll while text is shown ends the displayed message early: redrawBGAreas calls stopTalk.
While the TTS engine is speaking, displayDialog treats the message as still delayed, which extends it past _talkDelay.
Shrinks only the wall-clock wait per frame. Jiffy and frame counts are unchanged.

rows.notes: One row. descumm reports no sub-ops. The 252/253/254/other value is a routing parameter. The Pos/Color/Clipped/Center/Left/Overhead/Text items are a cumulative modifier list, not alternative sub-operations; MI1 uses only these and never Erase or SayVoice. In MI1, print(252,...) appears in 13 lines: debug or error text, a Y/N debug prompt whose key is then tested, and one Color-only default setter. print(253,...) appears in 31 lines (debug log text). With an actor that is not in the current room, actorTalk still converts the message into _charsetBuffer (actor.cpp:3469) before it returns (actor.cpp:3491-3511). Nothing is shown and VAR_HAVE_MSG and VAR_TALK_ACTOR are untouched, so a following o5_wait for the message returns at once unless another message is still running. If one is, its remaining pages are read from the overwritten buffer at the old _charsetBufPos. Talk timing: one page lasts 60 + n_chars*VAR_CHARINC jiffies after it starts displaying. The frame order is fixed. _talkDelay is decremented at the top of scummLoop (scumm.cpp:3134). VAR_HAVE_MSG is mirrored from _haveMsg in scummLoop_updateScummVars (scumm.cpp:3198, 3381-3382), before runAllScripts (scumm.cpp:3231). displayDialog runs after walkActors (scumm.cpp:3288). So scripts see VAR_HAVE_MSG drop to 0 on the frame after the one in which stopTalk runs. The repo plan pins enhancements=0 (docs/plan.md:504), so every enhancement-gated colour fix is off.

writes.detail: Result variable += operand. The target can be a global var or a script-local var (descumm forms Var/Local), with optional indirect indexing (0x2000) through another var. The operand is a constant or a var.

If the result operand is a bit variable (0x8000), readVar returns 0/1 and writeVar sets the bit when (bit + operand) != 0. The encoding allows this, but MI1's descumm forms for add show only Var and Local.

writeVar side effects on special engine vars. Writing VAR_CHARINC with a value in 0..9 writes the talkspeed config; in room 0 with a user override, the value is replaced by the user's setting. Writing VAR_NOSUBTITLES (v5 var 60) sets the subtitles config, and asserts that the value is 0 or 1, so any other sum aborts the engine. Reading VAR_NOSUBTITLES returns !subtitles config.

writes.detail: Starts a walk. Sets _walkdata.dest/destbox, destdir = -1, curbox, and _moving = (_moving & MF_IN_LEG) | MF_NEW_LEG, so _moving is nonzero at once. The destination is first snapped to the nearest walkable box point (adjustXYToBeInBox, threshold passes 30/80/0), or kept raw if _ignoreBoxes. Nothing more happens if the actor is already moving to the same snapped destination, or already stands on it.

For an actor in the current room with _ignoreBoxes set, _walkbox is set to kInvalidBox (kNewInvalidBox = 0 for v5 games without GF_SMALL_HEADER) at once. This happens before the 'already there' check, so it applies even when no walk follows.

Actor in the current room: walkActors moves _pos one step per frame along the box path (getNextBox), changes _walkbox per box, and on arrival sets _moving = 0 and setBox(destbox). The first step is taken in the same scummLoop iteration: walkActors runs after runAllScripts and the sentence script, and the first walkActor call already steps through calcMovementFactor -> actorWalkStep. If the destination box cannot be reached, the actor stops where it is (destbox = current box).

rows.notes: This is the main room-transition cause in v5. One opcode changes room, ego position and facing, every actor's visibility and box placement, camera, script population (exit, kill, entry) and message state. Execution order: putActor(room) -> VAR_WALKTO_OBJ = obj -> startScene [stopTalk, fadeOut, VAR_NEW_ROOM, exit scripts, kill room/object/local scripts, hide all actors, room load, ego to object (shown and box-snapped), showActors (box-snaps every actor in the room), entry scripts, ego re-place] -> VAR_WALKTO_OBJ = 0 -> camera follow (inventory script) -> optional walk. These steps after startScene run even if the caller was killed. Both object-not-in-room and cutscene-in-killed-caller are hard errors, not soft failures.

writes.detail: camera._mode = follow, camera._follows = actor, _movingToActor = false. If the actor's strip is outside the left/right trigger strips, setCameraAt sets camera._dest.x = actor x. Because the mode is already follow, camera._cur.x jumps there only when the distance is more than half the screen width; otherwise moveCamera pans the camera to dest at 8 px per frame. cur.x is clamped to VAR_CAMERA_MIN_X/MAX_X in setCameraAt, and dest.x in moveCamera. From then on, moveCamera pans toward the actor every frame whenever it leaves the trigger zone. VAR_CAMERA_POS_X is mirrored each frame.

Unlike loadRoomWithEgo, no actor is placed at an object and VAR_WALKTO_OBJ is not set. Then cur.x = actor x and setCameraAt run, so the camera starts on the actor.

Only on that room change: every actor visible in the old room is hidden, and a walking one gets _moving = 0 and its stand frame. Every actor of the new room, the followed one included, is shown through showActor/adjustActorPos: it is snapped into the nearest walk box, and _walkbox, scale and _moving = 0 are set. Apart from this snap, the followed actor keeps its own coordinates.

Only on that room change: exit scripts run, then room-object (WIO_ROOM, WIO_FLOBJECT) and room-local (WIO_LOCAL) scripts are killed. That includes the caller if it is one of these, with error() if it has an active cutscene or override. Global and inventory-object scripts survive. Then the entry scripts run.

The current message ends through stopTalk: _haveMsg = 0 (mirrored to VAR_HAVE_MSG next frame) and VAR_TALK_ACTOR = 0xFF. This happens on a room change; in setCameraAt when camera._cur.x differs from the last drawn camera._last.x while text is on screen (_charset->_hasMask); and in any later frame in which a follow pan moves the camera while text is shown, because v4-6 redrawBGAreas makes the same check.

writes.detail: Result var = pixel width of string resource N in the current charset. Starts at 1 for v>=4 (except FT). Measuring stops at the end, at a newline (10) or carriage return (13), or at embedded 0xFF/0xFE codes 1, 2, 3 or 9. It skips '@', the 2-byte parameters of codes 10, 12, 13 and 21, and the spaces after code 8. Code 14 switches the charset during the measurement, and the charset is restored at the end. Codes 4-7 (var, verb, name, string) are not expanded, so their bytes are measured as glyphs.

Prefill's 'starts' hit at script_v5.cpp:3298 is isScriptInUse, which only reads. walkActors advances only actors in the current room (actor.cpp:475-480).

What clears _moving:
- A room change hides all actors (room.cpp:111-113), and hideActor stops a visible actor (actor.cpp:2174-2181).
- putActor to another room hides a visible actor (actor.cpp:1765).
- putActor into the current room stops a walk (actor.cpp:1753-1758), or shows an invisible actor, and showActor also stops it (actor.cpp:1768-1769, actor.cpp:2238).
- startWalkActor on an out-of-room v5 actor only teleports it and never sets _moving (actor.cpp:866-872).

Two paths can still leave _moving set on an actor that walkActors skips:
- o5_putActorInRoom writes _room directly and does not stop a walk (script_v5.cpp:2193-2195).
- An invisible in-room actor that is walking when the room changes keeps _moving, because hideActor returns early for invisible actors (actor.cpp:2175-2176).
A WaitForActor on such an actor would not return until something else clears _moving. I derived this from the code; I did not observe it in a run.

read_back_by lists only opcodes that read the written state itself. No v5 opcode reads box flags, so it is empty. The effects show up only through actor state: o5_getActorWalkBox, o5_getActorX/Y, o5_getActorFacing and o5_getActorMoving.

What the v5 base Actor consults (box flag constants are in boxes.h:36-41):
- 0x80 invisible: the box is skipped as a walk or placement target. The exception is a box that also has 0x20 set and an actor that does NOT have the player class (31). Such a box stays usable for non-player actors, while player-class actors still skip it (actor.cpp:2037-2041, actor.cpp:3890-3892). Takes effect immediately.
- 0x80 in routing: excludes the box from the neighbour graph only after createBoxMatrix (boxes.cpp:1099). Without that call, the room's stored BOXM still routes through it.
- 0x08/0x10 flips and the low 3 bits: constrain facing (actor.cpp:1440-1488, actor.cpp:2107-2111).
- _extraBoxFlags: forces direction (actor.cpp:1423-1437).
- 0x40 locked: read only by Actor_v2::walkActor and Actor_v3 pathing (actor.cpp:1283-1284, actor.cpp:1369), not by v5.

Persistence:
- Box flags reload from room data on every room load (room.cpp:542-596).
- rtMatrix is a dynamic resource type (resource.cpp:1465), and saveload saves non-static types (saveload.cpp:1787-1793). saveload.cpp never calls resetRoomSubBlocks, so the changed flags persist through a save and load.
- _extraBoxFlags is cleared on room load (room.cpp:555) and has no saveload entry, so it is lost on load.

writeVar: GID_SAMNMAX changes the value written to VAR_TIMER_NEXT in one script (script.cpp:766-778). GID_LOOM v3, in one script, changes actor 4's animation speed when VAR_TIMER_NEXT is written (script.cpp:786-791). Both need the timing enhancement.
version <= 3 stores bit vars inside _scummVars (script.cpp:642-656, script.cpp:811-819). GF_FEW_LOCALS masks the local index (script.cpp:670-674, script.cpp:835-839).
rows.notes: It can target engine VARs. Decrementing VAR_TIMER_NEXT changes frame length (scumm.cpp:2821). Writing VAR_CHARINC calls setTalkSpeed (script.cpp:734-753). In v5, VAR_NOSUBTITLES (vars.cpp:173-175) is redirected to the subtitles config and asserts the value is 0 or 1 (script.cpp:726-731), so decrementing it from 0 would assert. Any opcode taking a var operand can also read the result. In MI1 the forms are local (26) and global (2).

writes.detail: Result var = byte offset of the object's handler for verb entry b, or of its 0xFF default handler. 0 if there is no match or the object is not found.

reads: object_owner: owner table and inventory list (whereIsObject)
other: current room's loaded objects and the object's VERB table in its OBCD (room resource, rtFlObject for a flobject, or rtInventory)
game_specific: GID_MONKEY2 with the game-breaking-bug-fix enhancement: one inventory object returns 0 for one verb (script.cpp:189-192)

Verb-table parsing varies by version, GF_OLD_BUNDLE, GF_SMALL_HEADER, LOOM PC-Engine and v8. MI1 CD finds the VERB block, uses 3-byte entries and returns verboffs + offset (script.cpp:200-217, script.cpp:243-257).
rows.notes: Despite the name, it does not read the verb UI (_verbs[]). It reads the object's own verb table, through getOBCDFromObject (object.cpp:1339-1366, flobject branch at object.cpp:1356-1357). The 0xFF default entry matches any verb (script.cpp:246), so a nonzero result does not prove that the exact verb has its own handler. Objects that are neither in the inventory nor among the current room's loaded objects return 0 (object.cpp:351-379, script.cpp:194-195). So does any object at or above _numGlobalObjects.

reads: walk_boxes: corner coordinates of box b in the current room
game_specific: checkXYInBoxBounds: version > 4 treats a degenerate (line) box as containing points within 2 px (boxes.cpp:559-566). Version >= 7 uses a two-orientation test (boxes.cpp:575-586).
getBoxBaseAddr: GID_MANIAC NES guard, version <= 4 last+1 workaround, layout by version/GF_SMALL_HEADER (boxes.cpp:465-497)
Actor::kInvalidBox depends on GF_SMALL_HEADER: 255 for small-header games, 0 otherwise, which includes MI1 CD (scumm.cpp:2085, actor.h:96-97)
rows.notes:
Unused in MI1. Branches via jumpRelative on whether the point lies in the box (script_v5.cpp:1529, script_v5.cpp:402-410). derefActor errors fatally on an invalid actor (actor.cpp:2281-2293).

Box numbers:
- A negative box, or box Actor::kInvalidBox, gives false (boxes.cpp:524-525). In MI1 CD kInvalidBox is 0, so box 0 always tests false.
- Box 255 is kOldInvalidBox. getBoxBaseAddr returns null for it (boxes.cpp:460-461), and then assert(bp) fires in getBoxCoordinates (boxes.cpp:606).
- Other numbers at or above the box count hit assertRange (boxes.cpp:485).

The opcode never checks the actor's room. An out-of-room actor's stored position is tested against the current room's boxes. Box coordinates are room data that no v5 opcode changes.

reads: var: global _scummVars, including engine-maintained VAR_ slots such as VAR_ROOM, VAR_VIDEOMODE, VAR_MACHINE_SPEED and VAR_CURRENT_LIGHTS (script.cpp:621)
bit variable: v5 _bitVars, var numbers with 0x8000 (script.cpp:657-665)
local script variable: vm.localvar, var numbers with 0x4000 (script.cpp:669-706)
indexed variable: the 0x2000 form reads a second word or var as the index (script.cpp:573-580)
player config 'subtitles' when the var read is VAR_NOSUBTITLES (script.cpp:592-594)
comparand: a script constant or var (script_v5.cpp:1541, 377-381)
game_specific: _game.version <= 2: the left var number is one byte; v5 reads a word (script_v5.cpp:1536-1539).

GID_MONKEY_EGA / GID_MONKEY_VGA (v4 floppy MI1): in a specific script slot comparing VAR_ROOM, the comparison is forced true, under kEnhGameBreakingBugFixes or kEnhMinorBugFixes (script_v5.cpp:1550-1562). Not active for GID_MONKEY DOS CD.
GID_MONKEY2: a VAR_SOUNDCARD == 5 comparison is forced true (script_v5.cpp:1568-1569). Not MI1.
GID_MONKEY2 with GF_ULTIMATE_TALKIE: two object-comparison overrides, plus a line skip that writes a global var and a local var (script_v5.cpp:1578-1615). Not MI1.
GID_MANIAC v2 demo: comparand 180 becomes 100 (script_v5.cpp:1618-1619). Not MI1.
readVar: VAR_NOSUBTITLES is var 60 in v5 (vars.cpp:173-174). Reading it returns !ConfMan 'subtitles' instead of the stored value (script.cpp:592-594). Active for MI1 DOS CD.
readVar: the GID_MONKEY2 copy-protection var remap (script.cpp:583-587) and the GID_MONKEY2 Mac VAR_MACHINE_SPEED override (script.cpp:599-601) do not apply to MI1.
readVar: in v5, bit vars come from _bitVars. Version <= 3 packs bits into _scummVars instead (script.cpp:642-665).
rows.notes: A pure test with no state writes. The var value and the operand are both int16 (script_v5.cpp:1533, 1540-1541), so values compare after truncation to 16 bits. jumpRelative skips the next block when the condition is false (script_v5.cpp:408-409), so descumm's 'if (X == Y)' is the condition under which the block runs. This is the main opcode a script uses to read back var, bit or local state that other opcodes wrote, including engine-maintained VAR_ slots.

reads: var: global _scummVars, including engine VAR_ slots such as VAR_DEBUGMODE (script.cpp:621)
bit variable: _bitVars (script.cpp:657-665). This is the dominant form in MI1 ('if (!Bit[..])').
player config 'subtitles' when the var read is VAR_NOSUBTITLES (script.cpp:592-594)
game_specific: GID_LOOM on PC Engine, in a specific script slot with kEnhMinorBugFixes: when a specific bit var is 1 and VAR_HAVE_MSG is nonzero, it rewinds the script pointer and calls o5_breakHere. That yields one frame and re-runs the test, which simulates a wait for the message (script_v5.cpp:1775-1784). Not MI1, so for MI1 the path is a = getVar() (script_v5.cpp:1786).

readVar guards are the same as for o5_isEqual. VAR_NOSUBTITLES (v5 var 60, vars.cpp:173-174) returns the config value (script.cpp:592-594) and is active for MI1. The MI2-only remaps at script.cpp:583-587 and 599-601 do not apply.
rows.notes: A pure test. The block runs when the var is 0, because jumpRelative(a == 0) skips it otherwise (script_v5.cpp:1789, 408-409). a is a full int, not int16 (script_v5.cpp:1757). In MI1 this is the main read-back opcode for bit variables.

writes.detail: Result var (MI1 always uses VAR_RESULT; in general any global, bit, local or indexed var named by getResultPos) is set to 1 if a matching global or local script slot is alive, else 0. Under the MI1 cutscene workaround (see game_specific) it is then overwritten with 1.

MI1 JollyRoger workaround (needs kEnhVisualChanges, off by default): when its conditions hold and the checked script is not running, a specific actor is moved to room 0 with Actor::putActor(0), which keeps its x/y and sets _room = 0.
writes.cite: script_v5.cpp:1478, script_v5.cpp:3901-3927, actor.h:217-219, actor.cpp:1741-1743, script_v5.cpp:1320-1321, object.cpp:415-422, object.cpp:536-540

writes.detail: Same workaround: if the actor was visible, it is now outside the current room, so hideActor runs. That sets _visible = false and, if the actor was moving, stopActorMoving sets _moving = 0 and starts the stand frame.

Same workaround: if the actor was visible and was the talking actor, stopTalk runs. VAR_TALK_ACTOR becomes 0xFF and _haveMsg becomes 0, and scummLoop_updateScummVars copies _haveMsg into VAR_HAVE_MSG.

reads: script slots: number, where and status of every slot (script.cpp:1557-1563)
script number operand: constant byte or var (script_v5.cpp:1449, 371-375)
for the MI1 cutscene workaround: the current script number, _currentRoom, and each live slot's where and cutsceneOverride (script_v5.cpp:1467-1475)
for the JollyRoger workaround: _roomResource, whether the current script is the room entry script, and actor existence (script_v5.cpp:3901-3926)
for the JollyRoger side effects: the actor's _visible and _moving, and the talking actor (actor.cpp:1731, 1753, 2178)
game_specific: GID_MONKEY, in a specific script slot in a specific room, with kEnhGameBreakingBugFixes: the result is forced to 1 while any live inventory-object script slot has an active cutscene/override. This makes the game script wait instead of hitting the fatal 'Object stopped with active cutscene/override' error (script_v5.cpp:1467-1476). kEnhGameBreakingBugFixes is in the default 'enhancements' value (engines/engine.cpp:201, engines/enhancements.h:120), so this is active for MI1 DOS CD in a default setup.

workaroundMonkey1JollyRoger applies to GID_MONKEY_EGA, GID_MONKEY_VGA, and GID_MONKEY without GF_ULTIMATE_TALKIE (so DOS CD qualifies). It needs a specific room's entry script (kScriptNumENCD) and kEnhVisualChanges. It only fires when _opcode == 0x68, the immediate-byte form; the 0xE8 var form never matches. The expected script number depends on _game.version == 5 (script_v5.cpp:3901-3927). kEnhVisualChanges belongs to kEnhGrp2, which is not in the default value kEnhGameBreakingBugFixes | kEnhGrp1 (engines/enhancements.h:123, 167-168; engines/engine.cpp:201), so it is off in a default setup. The legacy enable_enhancements=true key turns all groups on (engines/engine.cpp:202-206).
rows.notes: isScriptRunning reports only WIO_GLOBAL and WIO_LOCAL slots whose status is not ssDead (script.cpp:1557-1563). Frozen slots (status|0x80) and delayed or paused slots still count as running. Object verb scripts (WIO_ROOM, WIO_INVENTORY, WIO_FLOBJECT) are never reported. So this opcode reads back the lifecycle of global and room-local scripts, but not of object scripts or freezing. Enhancement defaults, checked: 'enhancements' defaults to kEnhGameBreakingBugFixes | kEnhGrp1 (engines/engine.cpp:201). So the MI1 cutscene workaround is on by default and the JollyRoger workaround (kEnhVisualChanges) is off by default. The JollyRoger write happens after setResult and never changes the result (script_v5.cpp:1450, 1478).

writes.detail: _objectOwnerTable[obj] = owner (byte 0..255). A nonzero owner does not add obj to the _inventory list. For an object in _inventory, getObjectOrActorXY (used by getDist) takes the position of the owning actor, so the new owner changes o5_getDist results.
writes.cite: object.cpp:172, object.cpp:301-304, object.cpp:77-95, script.cpp:194, object.cpp:361-367, object.cpp:425-441, script_v5.cpp:1406-1421

writes.detail: owner == 0 and obj in _inventory: the entry is removed, its rtInventory resource is nuked, and for version >= 4 the list is compacted, which shifts findInventory indices.

owner == OF_OWNER_ROOM (0x0F in v5): clearOwnerOf does not run, so if obj sat in _inventory it stays in the _inventory array. whereIsObject, getOBCDOffs and getOBCDFromObject then look for obj only in the current room's _objs list (WIO_ROOM or WIO_FLOBJECT if it is there, WIO_NOT_FOUND otherwise). getInventoryCount and findInventory stop counting it for its previous owner, because they match on the owner.
writes.cite: object.cpp:132, object.cpp:172, scumm.cpp:1742-1745, object.cpp:361-378, object.cpp:1325-1336, object.cpp:81, object.cpp:92, script.cpp:194

writes.detail: owner == 0 while the previous owner is OF_OWNER_ROOM: if obj is a floating object in the room's local object list, that entry is cleared and its rtFlObject is nuked.

owner == 0: stops every live object-script slot of obj (where is ROOM, INVENTORY or FLOBJECT) and its nested entries. If the calling script is one of them, it is killed too: _currentScript becomes 0xFF, so the rest of the caller never runs. In v5, stopping one that has an active cutscene/override calls error().

Runs the global script in VAR_INVENTORY_SCRIPT, if nonzero, with Local[0] = 0 in v5. It is non-recursive, so a running instance is stopped first. In v5 that stop calls error() if the instance has an active cutscene/override. If the caller is itself the inventory script, the stop kills the caller, and execution does not return to it.
writes.cite: object.cpp:106, object.cpp:173, script.cpp:901-907, script.cpp:65-66, script.cpp:271-280, script.cpp:356-358, script.cpp:390

reads: script operands: obj (word or var) and owner (byte or var) (script_v5.cpp:2725-2726)
object owner table: the previous owner (object.cpp:184)
room local object list _objs and fl_object_index (object.cpp:185-191)
current script slot's where and number (object.cpp:158-169)
script slots and nest entries of obj's object scripts (script.cpp:303-325)
slots and cutsceneOverride of a running inventory-script instance (script.cpp:270-275)

starts.what: VAR_INVENTORY_SCRIPT global script. It runs nested and synchronously inside this opcode until it yields, with Local[0] = 0 in v5. Any prior instance is stopped first; in v5 that is fatal if the prior instance has an active cutscene/override.
owner == 0: stops obj's running object verb scripts, including the calling script if it is one of them. In v5 this is a fatal error if one of them has an active cutscene/override.

game_specific: _game.version >= 6 passes obj as the inventory-script argument; v5 passes 0 (object.cpp:106).
GID_PASS and GID_HEGAME return early for obj == 0 in specific scripts (object.cpp:115-125). Not MI1.
Inventory gap compaction happens only for version >= 4 (object.cpp:204). Applies to v5.

stopObjectScript: for version >= 5, stopping an object script with an active cutscene/override calls error() (script.cpp:307-309). This applies to MI1, and the GID_MONKEY workarounds in o5_isScriptRunning and o5_setObjectName exist to avoid it.
stopScript: for version >= 5, stopping a global/local script with an active cutscene/override calls error() (script.cpp:273-275). This applies to the inventory-script restart.
OF_OWNER_ROOM is 0x0F for version < 7 (scumm.cpp:1742-1745).
rows.notes: A nonzero owner only rewrites the owner table. Adding to _inventory is o5_pickupObject's job (script_v5.cpp:2027-2028), so o5_getInventoryCount and o5_findInventory reflect owner changes only for objects already in _inventory, while o5_getObjectOwner always does. Moving a room object's owner off OF_OWNER_ROOM makes whereIsObject, getOBCDOffs and getOBCDFromObject stop treating it as a room object (object.cpp:361-367, 1325-1327, 1343-1345). o5_getVerbEntrypoint then returns 0 unless the object is in _inventory (script.cpp:194). findObject hit-testing does not check the owner (object.cpp:557-597). Setting the owner back to OF_OWNER_ROOM, a form MI1 uses, reverses this only if obj is in the current room's _objs, and it leaves any _inventory entry in place (object.cpp:361-376). The 'Odd setOwnerOf case' checks (object.cpp:158-169) run only after clearOwnerOf. If the caller was one of obj's own object scripts, stopObjectScript has already killed it and set _currentScript to 0xFF (object.cpp:133, 180; script.cpp:313-314), so ss is null and neither check fires; case #2 (caller number == obj, object.cpp:167-168) is unreachable. Case #1 (object.cpp:159-161) uses the calling inventory script's number as an _inventory index and is fatal if that entry is obj. Since clearOwnerOf has already removed obj from _inventory unless its previous owner was OF_OWNER_ROOM (object.cpp:184, 193-201), case #1 also needs that. If the nested inventory script freezes scripts, the caller is frozen and is not resumed when the inventory script yields (script.cpp:382-383, 928). assert(obj > 0) at object.cpp:130.

writes.detail: For each verb id in [a,b], the active slot (saveid 0) gets saveid = c. drawVerb then erases it because a saved verb is not drawn, and it becomes unclickable with its keyboard shortcut disabled.
verbMouseOver(0) clears the hover highlight. This is display only.

game_specific: Verb drawing guards in the path, none active for MI1 DOS: Mac GUI Indy3 skips drawing (verbs.cpp:1127), C64 pixel offsets (verbs.cpp:1124-1125), GID_FT skips mouse-over and the erase (verbs.cpp:993, 1190), and FM-Towns MI2/Indy4 and SegaCD Japanese MI1 background colour/clipping (verbs.cpp:1204, 1212).
rows.notes: No v5 opcode reads verb-slot state. o5_verbOps edits only the saveid-0 slot (script_v5.cpp:3140), and o5_getVerbEntrypoint is about object verbs. The effect gates player input: a saved verb can't be clicked or triggered by key (verbs.cpp:1018, 611), so runInputScript never reports that verb id. The switch tests the whole sub-op byte (script_v5.cpp:2649, 2655), so a var-parameter form (PARAM bits set in that byte) would fall to error() at script_v5.cpp:2691. descumm masks the byte with 0x1F (third_party/scummvm-tools/engines/scumm/descumm.cpp:3624) and would print such a form normally. Only constant forms work as implemented, and MI1 uses only constants. In MI1, saveVerbs is called from the script installed as VAR_CUTSCENE_START_SCRIPT, restoreVerbs from the VAR_CUTSCENE_END_SCRIPT script, and one other global script calls both.

writes.detail: For each verb id in [a,b] that has a slot saved under saveid c: the current active slot for that id (if any) is killed (verbid and curmode cleared, rtVerb nuked, erased). The saved slot then gets saveid = 0 and is redrawn. It is clickable and key-triggerable again only if its curmode is 1.
rtVerb resource of the killed active slot is nuked
verbMouseOver(0) clears the hover highlight

game_specific: killVerb redraws and resets hover only for version <= 6 when the slot is active (verbs.cpp:1321-1324). Applies to v5.
Same drawVerb, verbMouseOver and restoreVerbBG platform guards as saveVerbs (verbs.cpp:993, 1124-1127, 1190, 1204, 1212). None are active for MI1 DOS.
rows.notes: No opcode reads verb-slot state back. The effect is on which verb ids the player can produce through clicks and keys (verbs.cpp:1018, 611). As with saveVerbs, the full sub-op byte is switched on, so only constant-parameter forms reach this case (script_v5.cpp:2649-2655).

writes.detail: For each verb id in [a,b], the slot with saveid c is killed: verbid, curmode and saveid are cleared and rtVerb is nuked. It is erased only if c == 0, meaning an active verb.
rtVerb resource of the killed slot is nuked

game_specific: killVerb redraw applies only for version <= 6 with saveid 0 (verbs.cpp:1321-1324).
rows.notes: descumm prints this case as deleteVerbs (third_party/scummvm-tools/engines/scumm/descumm.cpp:3632). There are no uses in MI1 (prefill.json only lists saveVerbs and restoreVerbs). No read-back opcode.

writes.detail: Operand != 0 (freeze): every non-dead slot except the current one gets status |= 0x80 and freezeCount++. Freeze-resistant slots are skipped unless the operand is >= 0x80.
Freeze: every sentence-queue entry gets freezeCount++
Freeze: the slot that began the current cutscene is fully unfrozen (status &= 0x7F, freezeCount = 0). cutSceneScriptIndex is set only while beginCutscene runs VAR_CUTSCENE_START_SCRIPT.
Operand == 0 (unfreeze): each frozen slot gets freezeCount--, and 0x80 is cleared when the count reaches 0. Each sentence entry's freezeCount is decremented if > 0.

starts.what: Suspends every other live script slot (global, room-local and object scripts) that is not freeze-resistant, or all of them when the operand is >= 0x80. The scheduler runs only slots whose status is exactly ssRunning.
Suspends the sentence queue: checkAndRunSentenceScript does not start the sentence script while the top sentence is frozen.
Unfreeze (operand 0) resumes slots whose freezeCount reaches 0

cost_knobs.effect: Frozen scripts do not execute, and their o5_delay countdowns stop because decreaseScriptDelay only decrements slots whose status is exactly ssPaused. Their waits are lengthened by the time spent frozen.
When a nested script returns, its caller resumes only if the caller's freezeCount is 0

cost_knobs.knob: cutscene start/end scripts and the Esc override
cost_knobs.effect: In MI1 the freeze and unfreeze calls sit in the scripts installed as VAR_CUTSCENE_START_SCRIPT and VAR_CUTSCENE_END_SCRIPT, so the freeze lasts as long as the cutscene. Anything that ends the cutscene sooner (the override jump) also ends the freeze sooner.

game_specific: version <= 2: plain freeze and unfreeze with no counters and no sentence handling (script.cpp:917-923, 946-951)
The condition for freezing freeze-resistant slots is flag == 2 for version >= 7, else flag >= 0x80 (script.cpp:926). v5 uses >= 0x80.
freezeResistant is set from o5_startScript opcode bit 0x20 (script_v5.cpp:2971) and inherited by o5_chainScript (script_v5.cpp:850). o5_startObject passes 0 (script_v5.cpp:2889, script.cpp:145).
rows.notes: The freeze is a counter, so nested freezes need matching unfreezes. No comparison opcode can test it: o5_isScriptRunning still returns true for frozen slots (script.cpp:1557-1563). The only opcode that observes it is o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_SENTENCE, which stops waiting when the top sentence is frozen and the sentence script is not in use (script_v5.cpp:3297-3299). That is a wait condition, not a test, so it is not listed in read_back_by. A freeze does not affect scripts started later: runScript gives each new slot status ssRunning and freezeCount 0 (script.cpp:96, 100), so scripts started by input or other scripts during a freeze still run. MI1 uses only freezeScripts(127), below 0x80 so freeze-resistant scripts keep running, and freezeScripts(0).

writes.detail: c == 0: VAR_CURRENT_LIGHTS = a. The bit flags are LIGHTMODE_actor_use_base_palette, room_lights_on, flashlight_on and actor_use_colors. It is written directly with VAR(), bypassing writeVar.
c == 1: flashlight size _flashlight.xStrips = a, yStrips = b
_fullRedraw = true, always

reads: operands: a (byte or var), b and c (always direct bytes) (script_v5.cpp:1799-1801)
game_specific: v5 maps VAR_CURRENT_LIGHTS to var 9 (vars.cpp:168). It resets to base palette | actor colors | room lights on (vars.cpp:618).
getCurrentLights returns a constant for version >= 6 and uses _currentLights for v0. v5 reads the var (gfx.cpp:2051-2065).
drawFlashlight uses a different black on NES (gfx.cpp:1834-1836). Not MI1 DOS.
rows.notes: c values other than 0 and 1 only force a redraw. The engine consumes the lights var only for rendering, and only through getCurrentLights (gfx.cpp:2064 is the only engine read of VAR_CURRENT_LIGHTS). isLightOn decides whether room background strips are drawn or cleared to black (gfx.cpp:2067-2069, 1245, 1307, 2331, 2955). ClassicCostumeRenderer::setPalette, the v5 actor renderer, uses LIGHTMODE_actor_use_colors (costume.cpp:817). ScummEngine_v5::scummLoop_handleActors draws the flashlight when the room lights are off and the flashlight flag is on (scumm.cpp:4108-4110). In the engine code checked, no input or hit-testing code reads it; findObject has no light check (object.cpp:557-597). Unused in MI1 (lines_in_mi1 = 0), though MI1 reads VAR_CURRENT_LIGHTS once through o5_isEqual. Because it is an ordinary var, a script can also set it with o5_move.

reads: var: global _scummVars, including engine VAR_ slots such as VAR_VIRT_MOUSE_Y (script.cpp:621)
player config 'subtitles' when the var read is VAR_NOSUBTITLES (script.cpp:592-594)
comparand: a script constant or var (script_v5.cpp:1632)
game_specific: The handler has no game guards. The readVar guards are as for o5_isEqual: VAR_NOSUBTITLES (v5 var 60) returns the config value (script.cpp:592-594) and is active for MI1, while the MI2-only remaps (script.cpp:583-587, 599-601) are not.
rows.notes: a is the var and b is the operand, both int16 (script_v5.cpp:1631-1632). jumpRelative(b >= a) runs the block when operand >= var, which means var <= operand. That matches descumm's 'if (Local[0] <= 3777)'. The opcode name describes the operand side, not the var. A pure test with no writes.

reads: script bytecode: signed 16-bit jump offset fetched from the script (script_v5.cpp:407)

blocks.until: n/a. It only moves the instruction pointer and never yields. A backward jump makes a loop that yields only through an o5_breakHere or a blocking opcode inside the loop body.

rows.notes: Unconditional jump: o5_jumpRelative calls jumpRelative(false), so `_scriptPointer += offset` always runs (script_v5.cpp:1792-1794, 402-410). It changes only the VM's control flow (the current script's instruction pointer), never game state, so writes is empty on purpose. descumm prints it as goto / else / loop forms (prefill: goto 967, else 860, '/*' 246). The jump offset is read with ScummEngine::fetchScriptWord so the code also works for v0 (comment at script_v5.cpp:403-406). The function itself has no game guards. Separately, o5_isLessEqual calls o5_jumpRelative under a GID_INDY3 FM-Towns workaround (script_v5.cpp:1651-1657), which does not affect DOS MI1.

writes.detail: Global variable chosen by the result-var word (getResultPos; can be indexed through the 0x2000 form, base + var or immediate offset) becomes old value minus operand (16-bit immediate or variable). _scummVars[var] = value. In v5 two targets have side effects: VAR_CHARINC (var 37, vars.cpp:72) calls setTalkSpeed(9 - value) when 0..9, except in room 0 with a user talkspeed set, where the user's setting replaces the written value (script.cpp:734-754). VAR_NOSUBTITLES (var 60, vars.cpp:174) writes the ConfMan 'subtitles' option (script.cpp:726-731), but first asserts the value is 0 or 1 (script.cpp:730), so a subtraction leaving any other value there fails that assert; readVar returns that config value (script.cpp:592-594). If the target is any other engine-read VAR_ variable, the change takes effect when the engine next reads it.
If the result-var word has bit 0x8000, a bit variable in _bitVars is set to (old - operand) != 0. This is the v5 path; the version <= 3 path shares memory with _scummVars and does not apply to MI1.

If the result-var word has bit 0x4000, the current script slot's local variable becomes old - operand (index masked 0xFFF; MI1 lacks GF_FEW_LOCALS, detection_tables.h:199). Only the same script slot can read it back, and it is gone when that slot dies.

reads: var (current value of the result variable via readVar)
script bytecode (result-var word, optional index word)
game_specific: readVar: GID_MONKEY2 redirects var 490 to 518 (script.cpp:584) and forces VAR_MACHINE_SPEED=2 on Mac (script.cpp:599). Not MI1.
writeVar: GID_SAMNMAX (script.cpp:766) and GID_LOOM version < 4 (script.cpp:786) rewrite VAR_TIMER_NEXT writes. Not MI1.

readVar/writeVar: the version <= 3 bit-var layout (script.cpp:642, 811), HE room vars for heversion >= 80, GF_FEW_LOCALS (script.cpp:670, 835), and the HE-only VAR_SUBTITLES/NOSUBTITLES guards (script.cpp:721, 728) do not apply to DOS MI1 (v5, flags GF_AUDIOTRACKS only, detection_tables.h:199).
rows.notes: Pure arithmetic. The value is readVar(_resultVarNumber) - operand, and getResultPos has already stripped 0x2000 so readVar does not fetch again (script_v5.cpp:383-396, 3129). In MI1, prefill shows 589 Var-form and 37 Local-form uses; a grep of opcode bytes 0x3A/0xBA in data/scripts-dos-cd gives the same 626 lines, and none targets an engine-named VAR_ variable. The only side effects inside writeVar are the VAR_CHARINC (text speed) and VAR_NOSUBTITLES special cases. They change a later text cost, not the cost of this opcode.

writes.detail: Operand N != 0: every live slot running global/local script N (where WIO_GLOBAL or WIO_LOCAL) gets number=0 and status=ssDead. If that slot is the current one, _currentScript=0xFF and the calling script stops executing. Nest-stack entries record suspended callers (runScriptNested stores the caller's number, where and slot). stopScript clears the entries whose number is N, so if N was suspended because it had run another script nested, N is not resumed when that callee returns. The resume check would fail anyway on the dead slot; clearing matters only if a new instance of N reuses that slot meanwhile. A script that itself ran N nested is still resumed normally when N stops. Object verb scripts are never matched; o5_stopObjectScript handles those.
read_back_by: o5_wait (SO_WAIT_FOR_SENTENCE, only when N is VAR(VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT))
writes.cite: script_v5.cpp:3035-3038; script.cpp:262-293; script.cpp:354-365; script.cpp:377-390; script.cpp:1557-1563; script_v5.cpp:3296-3301

writes.detail: Operand 0 from a global/local script: stopObjectCode kills the current slot (number=0, ssDead, _currentScript=0xFF). The current script ends here.

Operand 0 from an object verb, inventory or FLObject script: stopObjectCode calls stopObjectScript(current object number), which kills every live slot running that object's code (where WIO_ROOM, WIO_INVENTORY or WIO_FLOBJECT) and clears matching nest entries. No v5 opcode can test object-script running state: isScriptRunning checks only GLOBAL/LOCAL, and isRoomScriptRunning is not called by any v5 opcode.

reads: var or immediate byte operand (script number, getVarOrDirectByte)

starts.what: Stops all running instances of global/local script N (operand != 0) and removes N's suspended-caller entries from the nest stack. Scripts that N had started run in their own slots and are not stopped.
Operand 0 stops the current script. If the current script is an object/verb/inventory script, every running instance of that object's script stops.

Indirect: when N is VAR(VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT), the dead slot lets the engine's checkAndRunSentenceScript, which runs every loop after runAllScripts and checkExecVerbs, pop and start the next queued sentence in the same frame. MI1 has 2 stopScript(VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT) statements.

blocks.until: n/a. The opcode never waits. When it stops the current script, the executeScript loop exits (_currentScript == 0xFF) and the script never resumes; that is termination, not blocking. The only yielding path is the GID_INDY4 workaround.

game_specific: GID_INDY4 with kEnhRestoredContent, under specific script/room/owner/class conditions and while VAR(VAR_HAVE_MSG) is set, rewinds the script pointer and calls o5_breakHere. The stop is retried every frame until the current message ends (script_v5.cpp:3023-3032). Not MI1.

Stopping a script whose slot has an active cutsceneOverride is a fatal error() when _game.version >= 5 (script.cpp:273-275; same for object scripts at script.cpp:307-309). stopObjectCode's global/local path errors for version >= 4 (script.cpp:879-880). These apply to MI1.
stopObjectCode has separate branches for version <= 2, <= 5 and >= 6 (script.cpp:868-896). MI1 uses the <= 5 branch, where operand 0 from an object script kills all instances of that object's script.

On the read-back path, o5_isScriptRunning has GID_MONKEY workarounds that apply to MI1. Under specific script/room conditions with kEnhGameBreakingBugFixes it forces result 1 while an inventory script in cutscene state runs (script_v5.cpp:1467-1476). It also calls workaroundMonkey1JollyRoger, which applies to GID_MONKEY without GF_ULTIMATE_TALKIE in a specific room/script with kEnhVisualChanges and can putActor(0) (script_v5.cpp:1478, 3901-3903, 3926-3928).
rows.notes: The direct operand is a byte (getVarOrDirectByte, script_v5.cpp:3021). The stop only clears slot number/status and nest entries (script.cpp:276-290). It undoes nothing the stopped script did (freeze counts, cutscene stack, actors and so on are not touched on this path). As a legality constraint, stopping a script inside an active cutscene/override is a fatal error in v5, so a valid route never does it. nukeArrays is a no-op for non-HE games (script.cpp:404-405). MI1 forms by opcode bytes 0x62/0xE2: 317 stopScript with an immediate number (111 of them stopScript(0)) and 2 with VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT.

writes.detail: The global result variable gets the object's owner-table entry. That is an actor number when the object is in that actor's inventory, or OF_OWNER_ROOM (0x0F in v5) when it lies in a room. It can also be 0 after setOwnerOf(obj, 0), or any 0..0xFF value a script stored through o5_setOwnerOf/putOwner. Initial owners are the low nibble of the DOBJ table (OF_OWNER_MASK 0x0F). All 142 MI1 uses write global var 0, the VAR_KEYPRESS slot in ScummVM's v5 var table (vars.cpp:37, not reassigned by ScummEngine_v5::setupScummVars, vars.cpp:164-176); descumm prints it as VAR_RESULT. The writeVar special cases (VAR_CHARINC, VAR_NOSUBTITLES) apply only if one of those were the target.

If the result-var word has 0x4000, a local variable of the current slot is set. Only the same slot can read it back. MI1 does not use this.

reads: var or immediate word operand (object number)
game_specific: OF_OWNER_ROOM is 0xFF for version >= 7 and 0x0F otherwise (scumm.cpp:1742-1745). MI1 gets 0x0F.
readVar/writeVar guards (GID_MONKEY2 at script.cpp:584 and 599, GID_SAMNMAX at 766, GID_LOOM at 786, version <= 3 bit vars at 642 and 811) do not apply to DOS MI1.
rows.notes: This is the read-back opcode for object ownership. The owner table is written by putOwner (object.cpp:301-305), reached from setOwnerOf (object.cpp:98-172; used by o5_setOwnerOf) and from o5_pickupObject (script_v5.cpp:2028). Initial owners come from the DOBJ global-object table (resource.cpp:1369-1370). getOwner range-checks the object (object.cpp:297), so an out-of-range number is a fatal error. Apart from the result write there are no side effects. The result slot (global var 0) is shared: the engine also writes it when a text-slot-3 message dialog is shown (printString case 3 -> showMessageDialog, string.cpp:118-119, 163-169), and o5_expression case 6 reads it back (script_v5.cpp:1182-1185), so a script must test it right after this opcode. MI1 operand forms by opcode bytes 0x10/0x90: 126 immediate, 14 local, 1 VAR_ME, 1 global var.

writes.detail: The chaining script's own slot is killed directly (number=0, status=ssDead, _currentScript=0xFF). Unlike stopScript or stopObjectCode, there is no cutsceneOverride check, and other instances of the same script or object are not stopped.
read_back_by: o5_isScriptRunning (only if the chaining script is global/local)

writes.detail: Global/local script N starts in a free slot with status ssRunning and cycle 1, and freezeResistant and recursive copied from the old slot. If the old slot was not recursive, any running instance of N is stopped first. A local N must exist in the current room or the engine raises a fatal error.
read_back_by: o5_wait (SO_WAIT_FOR_SENTENCE, only when N is VAR(VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT))

writes.detail: The new script's local variables 0..NUM_SCRIPT_LOCAL-1 are filled from the argument list (each a 16-bit immediate or a variable); the remaining locals are zeroed. Only the new script can read them.
A global N's script resource is loaded or locked through getResourceAddress. This touches the resource cache only and has no logic effect.
