starts.what: Runs script N immediately, nested in the same frame, until it first yields or ends. It is global if N < _numGlobalScripts and otherwise a local script of the current room.
Ends the chaining script itself. Its slot is freed before getScriptSlot runs, so N may reuse the same slot.
If the chaining slot was not recursive, stops other running instances of N.
With N = 0, runScript returns without starting anything, so chainScript(0) only ends the current script.

blocks.until: n/a. The chained script starts in the same frame. The chaining script never resumes: its nest entry has number 0, so runScriptNested leaves _currentScript at 0xFF afterwards.

game_specific: runScript workarounds for GID_MANIAC v0 demo and GID_ZAK version < 2 (script.cpp:49-60). Not MI1.
runScript takes its cycle from VAR_DEFAULT_SCRIPT_PRIORITY only for heversion >= 90 (script.cpp:88-89). Not MI1; MI1 cycle is 1.
runScriptNested allows a larger nesting limit for heversion >= 99 (script.cpp:351). Not MI1.

When the chaining slot is not recursive, the stopScript(N) inside runScript is a fatal error if a running instance of N has an active cutsceneOverride and _game.version >= 5 (script.cpp:65-66, 273-275). Applies to MI1.
rows.notes: Chaining costs zero frames. Each chain that runs before any yield adds one vm.nest level, because the chaining frame's runScriptNested has not returned yet. More than kMaxScriptNesting (15) open levels is a fatal error (script.cpp:351-352; script.h:116). Possible quirk, not traced to an effect: chaining clears neither the old slot's cutsceneOverride (script_v5.cpp:846-847) nor the new slot's, since runScript does not set it (script.cpp:93-102). endCutscene decrements the counter of the current slot (script.cpp:1650-1655), and abortCutscene resumes a slot by its saved index (vm.cutSceneScript, set by beginOverride). So chaining inside an active cutscene/override could leave a stale count on the old slot index, or let a new script that reuses that slot inherit it. Whether N runs the sentence script affects the engine too: while N == VAR(VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT) runs unfrozen, checkAndRunSentenceScript does not start the next queued sentence (script.cpp:1186-1191). In MI1, opcode bytes 0x42/0xC2 give 51 uses with 0 to 3 arguments (11 none, 9 one, 11 two, 20 three), mostly local variables passed through.

writes.detail: Fills the rectangle (x,y)-(x2,y2) (swapped if reversed, inclusive) with palette index 'color' in the front pixel buffer of the virtual screen that contains y: the main room view, the verb/inventory area or the text area. It is clipped to that virtscreen and marked dirty (dirtybit 0) so it reaches the display at the next screen update. On the DOS MI1 path the background buffer is not written, so a later restore of those strips from the background can overwrite the box (not traced). No opcode can read pixels back, so this cannot gate game logic.

reads: var or immediate word operands x, y, x2, y2 and byte color (a second opcode byte holds the parameter flags for x2/y2/color, script_v5.cpp:1023)
virtual screen layout (_virtscr topline, w, h via findVirtScreen)

blocks.until: n/a. Draws immediately; the display picks it up at the next frame's screen update.

game_specific: Version 8 uses a separate unclipped fill path (gfx.cpp:1430-1448). Not MI1.
Amiga GID_INDY4 remaps color through the room or verb palette (gfx.cpp:1452-1457). Not MI1.

FM-Towns: version 3 skips dirty marking (gfx.cpp:1507-1509); color >= 254 is special for GID_MONKEY2 and GID_INDY4 (gfx.cpp:1518-1528); the fill goes to the text/banner layer, and only GID_MONKEY or version 3 text falls through to the main buffer (gfx.cpp:1576-1609). FM-Towns MI1 only, not DOS.
HE heversion >= 60 and >= 72 interpret color as flag modes (gfx.cpp:1539-1570). Not MI1.
GF_16BIT_COLOR uses the 16-bit palette (gfx.cpp:1572-1573). Not MI1.
_macScreen exists only for Macintosh (scumm.cpp:1261-1267); there the text-surface mask is also cleared (gfx.cpp:1612-1615). Not DOS.
rows.notes: color == -1 takes a different path (gfx.cpp:1518-1537). On the main virtscreen it copies the background to the front buffer; on any other virtscreen it is a fatal error (gfx.cpp:1530-1531). An immediate byte cannot be -1, but a variable can, because getVarOrDirectByte returns getVar() (script_v5.cpp:371-375). This path is not live in MI1, whose colour variable only ever holds small positive constants. In MI1, opcode bytes 0x3F/0x7F/0xBF/0xFF give 21 uses in two forms. 18 are drawBox(0,0,319,199,0), which blanks to colour 0 the virtscreen containing y=0, clipped to it. 3 draw the band (0,140)-(319,160) with the colour from a local variable, clipped to the virtscreen containing y=140.

MI1's uses write global var 0, the VAR_KEYPRESS slot in ScummVM's v5 var table (vars.cpp:37, not reassigned by ScummEngine_v5::setupScummVars, vars.cpp:164-176); descumm prints it as VAR_RESULT. The writeVar special cases apply only if VAR_CHARINC or VAR_NOSUBTITLES were the target.

Besides the one direct statement that prefill counts, MI1 also runs this opcode nested inside an o5_expression (case 6 runs a nested opcode, then pushes _scummVars[0] whatever the encoded target, script_v5.cpp:1182-1185). That nested use is a second line in the decompiled scripts. Global var 0 is also written by the engine when a text-slot-3 message dialog is shown (string.cpp:118-119, 163-169).

writes.detail: The global result variable (getResultPos, indexed 0x2000 form allowed) becomes old value | operand (16-bit immediate or variable). The writeVar special cases for v5 still apply: VAR_CHARINC calls setTalkSpeed (script.cpp:734-754), and VAR_NOSUBTITLES asserts the value is 0 or 1 and writes the ConfMan subtitles option (script.cpp:726-731).
If the result-var word has 0x8000, the bit variable becomes (old | operand) != 0.
If the result-var word has 0x4000, a local variable of the current slot is set; only that slot can read it.

reads: var (current value of the result variable)
game_specific: readVar/writeVar guards (GID_MONKEY2 at script.cpp:584 and 599, GID_SAMNMAX at 766, GID_LOOM at 786, version <= 3 bit vars at 642 and 811, GF_FEW_LOCALS at 670 and 835) do not apply to DOS MI1.
rows.notes: Bitwise OR into the result variable. It has the same structure as o5_subtract and no other side effects. MI1's decompiled scripts never use it: prefill lines_in_mi1 = 0, and a grep for opcode bytes 0x57/0xD7 in data/scripts-dos-cd finds no statements and no '|=' forms. It is registered at opcodes 0x57 and 0xD7 (script_v5.cpp:150, 310).

writes.detail: Current slot running a global or room-local script ends in place: slot.number=0, status=ssDead. It does not call stopScript, so other slots or nest records holding the same script number are left alone.

Current slot running an object verb script (where = WIO_ROOM/WIO_INVENTORY/WIO_FLOBJECT): stopObjectScript(number) kills every live slot with that object number in an object context, not only the current one, and clears matching nested-call records.

reads: current script slot: where, number, cutsceneOverride

starts.what: Stops the current script. If it is an object script, it also stops all other live slots running a script of the same object.

Hands control back. If the ended script had been started nested from another script (runScript/runScriptNested), that caller resumes in the same frame, as long as it is still alive with the same number and where and has freezeCount 0.

Indirect: if the ended script is VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT, checkAndRunSentenceScript can pop and run the next queued sentence later in the same frame. The same applies to o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_SENTENCE, which stops waiting.

blocks.until: Not a wait. The script ends and never resumes: _currentScript=0xFF exits the executeScript loop.

game_specific: _game.version <= 2: global/local scripts end via stopScript(number), which kills all instances; object scripts end in place (script.cpp:868-874). Not v5.

_game.version 3..5 (includes MI1): object scripts go through stopObjectScript and global/local scripts end in place. Ending a global/local script with an active cutscene/override calls error(), which is fatal, only when version >= 4 (script.cpp:875-884).
stopObjectScript: stopping an object script that has an active cutscene/override is fatal only when version >= 5 (script.cpp:307-309). This applies to MI1.
_game.version >= 6: no stopObjectScript; only the current slot ends (script.cpp:885-895).
nukeArrays does work only for HE games (script.cpp:404-405).

GID_MONKEY workarounds outside this code path (o5_isScriptRunning script_v5.cpp:1466-1476; o5_setObjectName script_v5.cpp:2709-2716) wait on inventory scripts that have an active cutscene. This avoids the fatal 'stopped with active cutscene/override' error in stopObjectScript.

Indirect sentence pop (checkAndRunSentenceScript, reached when the ended script was the sentence script): GID_MONKEY, GID_MONKEY_EGA and GID_MONKEY_VGA with kEnhMinorBugFixes replace one specific give-to-actor sentence, whose object is still owned by the room, with a pick-up sentence when it is popped (script.cpp:1199; script.cpp:1283-1294). This applies to MI1 DOS CD when that enhancement is on.
rows.notes: Opcodes 0x00 and 0xa0 (script_v5.cpp:42, 242). descumm prints stopObjectCode() as the terminator of almost every script, so most of the 2022 MI1 lines are end-of-script markers, not explicit early exits. The same ending is also reached by o5_stopScript with operand 0 (script_v5.cpp:3035-3036). In v5 no opcode reports whether an object verb script is running: o5_isScriptRunning matches only WIO_GLOBAL/WIO_LOCAL (script.cpp:1561). Killing every slot of the same object number follows from the code; I did not check whether MI1 ever runs two verbs of one object at once.

writes.detail: Current slot: delay = 24-bit immediate operand (3 script bytes; always a constant, never a variable) and status = ssPaused. It then yields like breakHere: the script pointer is saved and _currentScript is set to 0xFF.

reads: immediate 24-bit operand from the script bytes
(during countdown) VAR_TIMER_NEXT via the main-loop delta

blocks.until: slot.delay goes below 0. Each frame, decreaseScriptDelay subtracts that frame's delta from every slot whose status is exactly ssPaused. delta is VAR_TIMER_NEXT, raised to at least 1 and capped at 15. When the delay goes negative, the slot becomes ssRunning and runs in that same frame's runAllScripts, because the countdown happens first. For a constant delta, frames waited = floor(delay/delta) + 1, so delay(0) behaves like one breakHere. Only this slot waits: if it was started nested from another script, the caller resumes at once in the same frame.

cost_knobs.effect: Frame length in jiffies (delta). The delay counts down by delta per frame, and each frame waits delta*4 quarter-frames of wall-clock time. Wall time is therefore about delay jiffies, while the frame count is about delay/delta. A value of 0 is treated as 1.
The per-frame decrement is capped at 15 even when VAR_TIMER_NEXT is larger, so delays stretch in wall-clock time when frames are longer than 15 jiffies.

cost_knobs.knob: freezeScripts (o5_freezeScripts, often called by the game's cutscene start script)
cost_knobs.effect: A frozen slot has status ssPaused|0x80, which fails the == ssPaused test, so its delay does not count down while frozen. Freeze-resistant slots are exempt unless the freeze flag is >= 0x80.

abortCutscene sets the override-owning slot to ssRunning at its override target and sets VAR_OVERRIDE=1, which ends a pending delay in that slot at once. This only works when an override is registered at the current cutscene level and VAR_CUTSCENEEXIT_KEY is not 0.
The per-frame sleep becomes 0 ms (fastMode&2 or speedrun skipWaits) or 10 ms (fastMode&1). This changes wall-clock time only, not the number of frames.
Sets how many milliseconds one jiffy/quarter-frame lasts. Wall-clock only.
A delay does not end while the TTS engine is speaking.

game_specific: o5_breakHere, which o5_delay calls at the end: GID_LOOM PC-Engine English in one specific script and room forces delay=120 (script_v5.cpp:825-828). Not MI1.
decreaseScriptDelay: GID_INDY3 Macintosh has a credits-text hook for one script when its delay expires (script.cpp:1527-1540). Not MI1.
Main-loop delta adjustments exist for version 0, GID_MANIAC v1, enhancement-gated INDY3/LOOM/ZAK name-entry rooms, and the v8 menu room (scumm.cpp:2844-2882). None apply to MI1.
FM-Towns smooth scrolling lowers delta through _scrollDeltaAdjust (scumm.cpp:2829-2832; gfx_towns.cpp:251). Not MI1 DOS.
Timer frequency is chosen per version and platform; v5 DOS uses the PIT orchestrator divisor scaled by the v5 subtimer threshold (scumm.cpp:3008-3010).
rows.notes: Opcode 0x2e (script_v5.cpp:99). The unit is the 60 Hz jiffy, the same unit as VAR_TIMER_NEXT. o5_delayVariable is the separate opcode that takes a variable operand. No opcode can tell a delayed script from a running one: o5_isScriptRunning only checks status != ssDead (script.cpp:1561). A room change kills WIO_ROOM, WIO_FLOBJECT and WIO_LOCAL slots even while they are paused, which cancels the delay; inventory-object (WIO_INVENTORY) and global slots survive the room change and keep counting (script.cpp:1088-1105). MI1 scripts set VAR_TIMER_NEXT to different values at different times, including 0, so the frame count for the same delay(N) is not constant.

writes.detail: Current slot's cutsceneOverride counter is incremented. While it is non-zero the slot must not end. These cases are fatal errors: the slot ends itself with stopObjectCode (global/local scripts from v4, object scripts from v5); it is stopped by stopScript or stopObjectScript (v5); or it is the current room, FLObject or local script that triggers a room change (v5). Other room and local slots swept at room exit only get a warning, and their counter is cleared. killAllScriptsExceptCurrent clears the counter silently. endCutscene and abortCutscene decrement it.

writes.detail: Cutscene stack push: cutSceneStackPointer+1 (overflowing kMaxCutsceneNum is fatal), cutSceneData[sp]=args[0], cutSceneScript[sp]=0, cutScenePtr[sp]=0. No override is registered at the new level yet. o5_endCutscene later passes args[0] to VAR_CUTSCENE_END_SCRIPT.
vm.cutSceneScriptIndex = calling slot while the start script runs, then 0xFF. During that time freezeScripts unfreezes the calling slot and resets its freezeCount.

reads: argument list (word args, constants or variables, via getWordVararg)

starts.what: If VAR_CUTSCENE_START_SCRIPT is non-zero, runScript runs that script with the cutscene args as its locals. The call is non-recursive (an existing instance is stopped first) and the script runs nested immediately.

blocks.until: Not a wait. The start script runs nested. When it ends or yields, the caller resumes in the same frame: cutSceneScriptIndex keeps the caller unfrozen if the start script freezes scripts. The cutscene state then lasts until o5_endCutscene, or until Esc when an override is registered.

cost_knobs.effect: o5_cutscene clears cutScenePtr at the new level, so Esc does nothing for this cutscene until the script runs o5_beginOverride. After that, Esc jumps the override owner to its override target and sets VAR_OVERRIDE=1. An override registered at an outer level cannot be reached while this level is active.

game_specific: GID_INDY3 FM-Towns, one specific room and script, with kEnhVisualChanges: forces args[0]=1 (script_v5.cpp:948-950). Not MI1.
runScript, used to start the cutscene start script: GID_MANIAC v0 demo and GID_ZAK v<2 workarounds (script.cpp:49-60). Not MI1.

The fatal 'ending or stopped with active cutscene/override' checks are version-gated: >= 4 for a global/local script ending itself (script.cpp:879), >= 5 for stopScript, stopObjectScript and room exit (script.cpp:273-275; script.cpp:307-309; room.cpp:61, 67). Both gates apply to MI1.

GID_MONKEY: o5_endCutscene has an MI1-specific workaround, workaroundMonkey1StorekeeperWaitTablesLine (script_v5.cpp:956-957). o5_isScriptRunning and o5_setObjectName have MI1 workarounds that read inventory slots' cutsceneOverride (script_v5.cpp:1466-1476; 2709-2716). None of these is in o5_cutscene's own path.
rows.notes: Opcode 0x40 (script_v5.cpp:122). In v5 the engine itself does not freeze scripts, hide the cursor or disable verbs when a cutscene begins; that is all up to the game's VAR_CUTSCENE_START_SCRIPT, which MI1's boot script sets. The args are passed through unchanged as that script's locals; descumm shows forms like cutscene([2]). No v5 opcode can test cutscene stack depth or cutsceneOverride. The only related state scripts can see is VAR_OVERRIDE, which this opcode does not set: o5_beginOverride and endCutscene set it to 0, and abortCutscene sets it to 1 (script.cpp:1660; 1706; 1723-1724).

reads: variable: global, bit or local, possibly indexed with 0x2000; the first operand is always a variable
both are truncated to int16 before comparing

blocks.until: Not a wait. It is a conditional relative jump only.

Comparisons use int16, so variables wider than 16 bits compare on their low 16 bits. This opcode only reads state: for the catalogue it is one of the read-back functions for any variable, never a cause. A test of VAR_NOSUBTITLES reads the user's ScummVM subtitle setting, not game state.

writes.detail: Walker's walk target, taken once from the target actor's position at call time: dest = (target actor x ± dist, target actor y), box-adjusted by adjustXYToBeInBox; destbox; destdir=-1; curbox=_walkbox; _moving = MF_NEW_LEG (MF_IN_LEG kept). dist is added when the target is left of the walker and subtracted otherwise. dist=255 means walker scaled width + half the target's scaled width. Nothing re-targets later, so a target that moves afterwards is not followed: the walker goes to where the target was. Nothing changes if the walker already stands at the adjusted point or is already walking there.

Each frame's walkActors steps the walker along the walk-box path, one step per frame, and updates _pos. walkActors runs after runAllScripts, so when the call comes from a script run in runAllScripts the first step happens in the same frame.

_walkbox is updated through setBox as boxes are crossed and on arrival. If the walker has _ignoreBoxes set, startWalkActor sets _walkbox = kInvalidBox at once and the walk is one straight leg. The scale (_scalex/_scaley) is recomputed from the box, or from its scale slot and the position, both by setBox and on every redraw; each walk step requests a redraw, so the scale can change along the walk. While _ignoreBoxes is set the scale is left alone.

Depends on the costume data: if a walk-animation frame carries costume command 0x78, soundCounter is incremented and playActorSounds starts the actor's _sound[0] that frame, unless _fastMode is set.

cost_knobs.effect: Per-frame step size along each leg.

The step is multiplied by scale/256, so actors scaled down cover fewer pixels per frame. The scale comes from the walk box or its scale slot on every redraw, so a scale set with o5_actorOps SO_ACTOR_SCALE lasts only while _ignoreBoxes is set.
The number of legs and their lengths follow the box matrix (getNextBox/findPathTowards).
One walk step per frame, and each frame lasts VAR_TIMER_NEXT jiffies of wall-clock time.

Shortens the per-frame sleep, which is wall-clock only; the step count is unchanged. _fastMode also skips costume footstep sounds in playActorSounds, and o5_isSoundRunning can see that difference. Speedrun skipWaits does not reach that path.

writes.detail: VAR_CAMERA_POS_X = _cur.x. It is written at once (the clamped operand) only when VAR_SCROLL_SCRIPT is non-zero; otherwise at the start of the next frame. By then the same frame's moveCamera has changed _cur.x: with VAR_CAMERA_FAST_X = 0 it rounds _cur.x down to a multiple of 8, and with VAR_CAMERA_FAST_X set it snaps _cur.x to the clamped _dest.x. cameraMoved then clamps it to the room's scroll range. So the value read back is the 8-aligned, clamped position, not always the operand. If moveCamera changed _cur.x and VAR_SCROLL_SCRIPT is set, the variable is rewritten in that frame too. A call made after moveCamera in the frame (for example from VAR_MAIN_SCRIPT) is seen unrounded for one frame.

writes.detail: Actor walk/turn flags (_moving), by v5 anim value. 252-255 (stop) sets _moving=0 and halts a walk where the actor stands. 244-247 (turn) sets _moving=MF_TURN, which overwrites the walk bits, so a walk in progress is abandoned. 248-251 (face now) clears only the MF_TURN bit. Each of these _moving writes happens only when the actor is in the current room.

248-251: _facing is set at once to dir = oldDirToNewDir(anim&3) (0->270, 1->90, 2->180, 3->0). Nothing happens if the actor already faces that way. The write happens even when the actor is in another room; only the costume update is skipped. If the actor is mid-walk (face-now keeps the walk bits), the next walk step steers _facing back toward the leg's _targetFacing via updateActorDirection(true)/setDirection. That step runs in the same frame's walkActors, so the change does not stick. 244-247: _targetFacing is set. walkActors then calls setDirection one interpolation step (90 degrees) at a time until _facing equals the remapped target, then clears _moving; the first step comes in the same frame as the opcode. In v5, Actor::remapDirection returns the target the turn converges on without rewriting _targetFacing. The remap uses the actor's walk-box flags or _extraBoxFlags, and the actor's XFlip/YFlip classes. It is skipped entirely when the actor has _ignoreBoxes set. Box flags 1-6 force a direction that snaps in one step, with no interpolation.

GID_MONKEY2 / GID_INDY3 / GID_LOOM workarounds; none apply to MI1 (script_v5.cpp:1068-1102).
rows.notes: descumm prints this form as plain drawObject(obj) with no sub-token; I counted 176 such lines in MI1. Any sub-op other than 1, 2 or 0x1F is a fatal error (script_v5.cpp:1056-1057). Nothing is written when the object is not in the current room (script_v5.cpp:1104-1106).

writes.detail: VAR_OVERRIDE = 0
The override target at this cutscene level is cleared (cutSceneScript/cutScenePtr = 0) and the cutscene stack is popped. After this, Esc's abortCutscene has nothing to jump to at this level.

The current script slot's cutsceneOverride count is decremented. It is decremented again only if an override pointer is still pending and the count is still above 0. In v5 a script or object that ends or is stopped with a nonzero count is a fatal error, so this must run before the script ends.
writes.cite: script.cpp:1654-1655, script.cpp:1662-1663, script.cpp:1634, script.cpp:879-880, script.cpp:273-274, script.cpp:307-308, room.cpp:61, room.cpp:67

reads: MI1 workaround only: room, script slot, game bits/vars, last speaking actor, VAR_OVERRIDE, VAR_HAVE_MSG

starts.what: The script numbered in VAR_CUTSCENE_END_SCRIPT, if nonzero, with args[0] = the first argument of the matching o5_cutscene. It is started non-recursively, so any running instance is stopped first, and it runs nested at once until it yields.

blocks.until: The engine proper never blocks here. The one exception is a ScummVM addition, not original behaviour: MI1 (GID_MONKEY_EGA, GID_MONKEY_VGA, and GID_MONKEY without GF_ULTIMATE_TALKIE, which includes DOS CD), one specific scene, with kEnhRestoredContent on. There, when VAR_OVERRIDE is 0 and VAR_HAVE_MSG is nonzero, the opcode rewinds and yields every frame until the message finishes, then runs normally.

cost_knobs.effect: abortCutscene jumps the cutscene script to the point recorded by o5_beginOverride and sets VAR_OVERRIDE=1, so endCutscene is reached sooner. The key does nothing when VAR_CUTSCENEEXIT_KEY is 0.
MI1 workaround wait only: sets the per-character talk delay, which decides how long VAR_HAVE_MSG stays set.
Zeroes _talkDelay, which ends the message and therefore the workaround wait early.
Frame period; _talkDelay drops by the frame delta each frame.

game_specific: GID_MONKEY_EGA/GID_MONKEY_VGA/GID_MONKEY (not GF_ULTIMATE_TALKIE), one room/script, kEnhRestoredContent, gated on specific game bits/vars and the last speaking actor: simulates a missing wait-for-message before ending the cutscene. This applies to MI1 DOS CD (script_v5.cpp:956-957, 3848-3884).
GID_ZAK FM-Towns, one room/script: a cutscene-stack underflow is ignored instead of being a fatal error (script.cpp:1676-1679).

_game.version >= 5: stopping a script or object with cutsceneOverride > 0 is a fatal error (script.cpp:273-274, 307-308). On leaving the room the error applies only to the current script, when it is a room-object or local script (room.cpp:58-69). Every other room-object or local script is killed with a warning and its count zeroed (script.cpp:1083-1102). killAllScriptsExceptCurrent also zeroes counts (script.cpp:1140). In v4-v5, ending a global or local script with a nonzero count is fatal (script.cpp:879-880).
GID_MONKEY workarounds in o5_isScriptRunning and o5_setObjectName read the cutsceneOverride counts of inventory-object scripts (script_v5.cpp:1467-1476, 2709-2716).
rows.notes: endCutscene decrements the count of the script that runs it, not necessarily the one that began the cutscene (script.cpp:1651). Running it with an empty cutscene stack is a fatal 'Cutscene stack underflow' error (script.cpp:1668-1681). The engine does not touch cursor, userput or verbs here; what the game's end script does depends on the game. o5_cutscene's beginCutscene is the only place the count is incremented (script.cpp:1634).

writes.detail: The result variable (global var, bit or local, chosen by the script) gets the object's state (0-255) from the global state table.

game_specific: GID_MANIAC (not v0, not NES) with copy protection off: getState forces the kObjectStateIntrinsic bit on two specific objects, so a read also writes. This cannot be reached through this opcode. Maniac exists only as v0-v2, and those engines' tables map 0x0f/0x8f to o2_ ops, not o5_getObjectState (object.cpp:310-322, detection_tables.h:159-167, script_v2.cpp:59, script_v2.cpp:219, script_v0.cpp:55, script_v0.cpp:215).
rows.notes: An object number outside 0.._numGlobalObjects-1 fails assertRange (object.cpp:308). This is the only v5 opcode that returns object state. o4_ifState/o4_ifNotState exist only in the v4 table (script_v4.cpp:45-53) and are commented out in v5 (script_v5.cpp:100, 140).

writes.detail: The result variable gets one of the following. 0 if the argument < 1. The actor's _pos.y if the argument < _numActors, with no room check. For an object: -1 if not found; walk_y if it is a room-owned object in the current room (v3-v5); the owning actor's y if it is an inventory object whose owner is an actor in the current room; otherwise -1.
writes.cite: script_v5.cpp:1359-1368, object.cpp:1648-1661, object.cpp:1620-1622, object.cpp:351-379, object.cpp:412-443, object.cpp:506-508, actor.h:280-282

game_specific: GID_INDY3 non-Macintosh reads the argument as a byte instead of a word (script_v5.cpp:1363-1366).
rows.notes: The actor branch cannot fail. isValidActor only checks 0 <= id < _numActors, and each actor's _number is its index, so derefActor on 1.._numActors-1 always succeeds (actor.cpp:2277-2279, actor.cpp:107-108, object.cpp:1653). Arguments >= _numActors take the object path, which has no fatal case. Object positions changed by drawObject setXY are visible here, because walk_y moves with them, but only while the object is room-owned (object.cpp:361-368).

writes.detail: The result variable gets the actor's _moving bitfield: 0 idle, MF_NEW_LEG=1, MF_IN_LEG=2, MF_TURN=4, MF_LAST_LEG=8 (MF_FROZEN=0x80 is set only by v6/v8 actorOps).

rows.notes: There is no room check. An actor number outside 0.._numActors-1 is a fatal error through derefActor (actor.cpp:2277-2279, actor.cpp:2286-2290). o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_ACTOR blocks on this same field, but uses derefActorSafe (script_v5.cpp:3281-3286).

writes.detail: The result variable gets the actor's _elevation.

rows.notes: _elevation is set by actorOps SO_ELEVATION (script_v5.cpp:506-507, actor.h:316-320). It is reset to 0 by initActor, which actorOps SO_DEFAULT reaches (script_v5.cpp:503-504, actor.cpp:194). An actor number outside 0.._numActors-1 is a fatal error through derefActor (actor.cpp:2277-2279, actor.cpp:2286-2290). MI1 uses this opcode on one line.

writes.detail: VAR_LAST_SOUND = the sound number (v5 VAR_LAST_SOUND is var 23).

The sound is added to the sound queue and triggered by processSound at the end of the frame; the queue is drained last-in first-out. While the sound is queued, isSoundRunning already reports it as running, unless it is the current CD sound, in which case pollCD is returned first.
writes.cite: sound.cpp:125, sound.cpp:128-138, scumm.cpp:4157, sound.cpp:140-159, sound.cpp:859-882, sound.cpp:866-867, sound.cpp:928-935

game_specific: FM-Towns with _game.version == 3 only: the opcode is a CD-audio status query that writes a result variable (CD poll, current CD track, CD volume) and starts nothing. MI1 FM-Towns is v5, so it is not affected (script_v5.cpp:2771-2800).
Unlike o5_startSound, it does not zero VAR_MUSIC_TIMER and has no game workarounds (script_v5.cpp:2802 vs script_v5.cpp:2828-2829).
rows.notes: Not used in MI1 (lines_in_mi1 = 0). The v5 opcodes are 0x02 and 0x82 (script_v5.cpp:44, 204); v0 and v2 tables reuse it (script_v0.cpp:39, script_v2.cpp:43). When the queued sound fires, triggerSound first checks replacement CD tracks, which are used only when _useReplacementAudioTracks is set (sound.cpp:196, soundcd.cpp:400-418). MI1 CD's own CD-audio sound resources (SOUN type 2) are played further down (sound.cpp:322-331).

writes.detail: New script slot, taken as the lowest dead slot from 1 up (all 80 slots in use is a fatal error). number = script argument, status ssRunning, where = WIO_GLOBAL if script < _numGlobalScripts, else WIO_LOCAL (a room-local script; error if the current room does not have it). freezeResistant = opcode bit 0x20 (descumm ',F'), recursive = opcode bit 0x40 (',R'), freezeCount 0, delayFrameCount 0, cycle 1.

Unless R is set, every live global or local instance with the same script number is killed first (status ssDead), and nest entries with that number are cleared, so a caller with that number further up the nest chain never resumes. In v5, killing a slot that holds an active cutscene override is a fatal error().

The new slot's local variables: Local[0..n-1] = the argument list (each item an immediate word or a variable); the remaining locals are zeroed. Scripts can address only Local[0..20] (assertRange), although NUM_SCRIPT_LOCAL is 25.

reads: script number (var or immediate byte) and argument list (vars or immediate words)
_numGlobalScripts and the current room's local-script offset table
existing script slots with that number (for the non-recursive kill, and their cutsceneOverride) and the nest stack
calling slot's number, where, status and freezeCount after the child returns (decides whether the caller resumes)

starts.what: The named global or room-local script. It runs nested at once (runScriptNested -> executeScript) until its first breakHere, delay or wait, or its end; then control returns to the caller in the same frame.
Stops all existing instances of the same script number unless the R bit is set.

blocks.until: Does not wait. The child runs synchronously first. The caller then continues in the same frame, but only if its slot still has the same number and where, is not dead, and has freezeCount 0. Otherwise _currentScript becomes 0xFF and the caller does not continue this frame: it is frozen, or, if it was killed, never.

cost_knobs.effect: freezeScripts skips a freeze-resistant slot unless its flag is >= 0x80. Such a script keeps running, and keeps counting down its delays, during a freeze. In v5 freezeScripts is reached only through o5_freezeScripts (a cutscene-start script may call it; beginCutscene itself does not freeze). A non-resistant paused slot gets status 0x81, and decreaseScriptDelay only counts down status == ssPaused.
Everything the child does before its first break runs inside the caller's frame, so no frame time passes.

game_specific: GID_LOOM v3 (enhancement) skips one script start; GID_ZAK FM-Towns (enhancement) skips one; GID_INDY3 (enhancement) rewrites the arguments of one IQ-points call; GID_LOOM v3 (enhancement) fills in a missing actor argument. None of these applies to GID_MONKEY DOS (script_v5.cpp:2910-2955).

With _copyProtection off: GID_LOOM DOS v3 redirects the copy-protection script, and GID_MONKEY_VGA and GID_MONKEY on kPlatformMacintosh suppress a copy-protection script start. None of these fires for GID_MONKEY DOS CD (script_v5.cpp:2958-2969).
GID_INDY3 saves the series IQ after a specific script runs (script_v5.cpp:2975-2976).

GID_MONKEY_VGA with kEnhRestoredContent: after a specific lava-maze script starts, an actor is initialised and put in the room as animated smoke. This is GID_MONKEY_VGA only, not the DOS CD release, whose own script already has the smoke (script_v5.cpp:2978-3006).
runScript has workarounds for the GID_MANIAC v0 demo and GID_ZAK v<2 (script.cpp:49-60), and a heversion>=90 cycle priority (script.cpp:88-89). None applies to MI1.
stopScript's fatal error for killing a slot with an active override applies to version >= 5, so it applies to MI1 (script.cpp:273-275).
rows.notes: op is saved before getWordVararg, which overwrites _opcode (script_v5.cpp:2896, 3437). Script 0 is a no-op (script.cpp:62-63). If a script restarts itself without R, stopScript kills the caller and sets _currentScript=0xFF (script.cpp:279-280), so the old instance never resumes. The child's didexec is set when it executes (script.cpp:507), so runAllScripts does not run it a second time in this frame (script.cpp:979). The locals can be tested only from inside the started script. Fatal limits: 80 script slots (script.cpp:339) and 15 nested scripts (script.cpp:351-352; script.h:116). The global script resource is loaded if needed (script.cpp:76). MI1 uses the plain (0x0A/0x8A), ',F' (0x2A), ',R' (0x4A/0xCA) and ',F,R' (0x6A/0xEA) forms.

writes.detail: actor._room = room argument. The stopTalk path below runs first, while _room still holds the old room. Apart from that path, a non-zero room writes no other actor field: no showActor or hideActor runs.
Only when room == 0: putActor(0,0,0) sets _pos = (0,0), sets _room = 0 again, and sets _needRedraw.

Only when room == 0 and the actor was visible: since it is no longer in the current room, hideActor runs. A walk is stopped (_moving = 0, stand frame), _visible = false, the costume sound counters are reset, and _needBgReset = true. No walk script is stopped, because v5 never sets _walkScript (only script_v6.cpp:2348 and script_v8.cpp:902 do).

Only when room == 0 and the actor is VAR_EGO: _egoPositioned = true. In v5 the only consumer is startScene. It clears the flag before running the entry script, and afterwards auto-places ego at the entry object only if the flag is still false and the scene was entered through loadRoomWithEgo. So this matters only when it runs inside an entry script during loadRoomWithEgo. The re-check in o5_loadRoomWithEgo is under version <= 4 and does not apply to MI1.
When the actor is visible, is the talking actor, and room != _currentRoom: stopTalk sets _haveMsg = 0, which is copied into VAR_HAVE_MSG every frame, and _talkDelay = 0, so the current message ends.
On the same stopTalk path: VAR_TALK_ACTOR = 0xFF, through setTalkingActor(0xFF).

On the stopTalk path, if the actor is in the current room and _useTalkAnims is set: the talk-stop animation starts (startAnimActor(_talkStopFrame); v5 never sets _talkScript), and _useTalkAnims = false. stopTalk runs before _room is written, so 'in the current room' refers to the actor's old room; since the actor is visible, this normally holds even when it is being sent to another non-zero room.
On the stopTalk path: _keepText = false and restoreCharsetBg() erase the message text from the screen. stopTalkSound also runs, but MI1 DOS CD has no speech.

reads: actor number and room (var or immediate byte)
actor _room before the write (isInCurrentRoom inside stopTalk and putActor)

cost_knobs.knob: Moving the talking actor out of the room
cost_knobs.effect: stopTalk zeroes _talkDelay and _haveMsg. A pending o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_MESSAGE then ends once VAR_HAVE_MSG is re-synced at the next frame's variable update, instead of waiting out the text time.

game_specific: GID_MONKEY2 on kPlatformMacintosh (kEnhRestoredContent): one actor's placement in room 0 is changed into an in-room actor setup. Not MI1 (script_v5.cpp:2181-2191).

In putActor: a GID_SAMNMAX position fix, heversion>=62 and >=71 handling, a v0 walk reset, and a GID_MANIAC v<=1 facing reset. None applies to MI1 (actor.cpp:1738-1739, 1746-1747, 1761-1764, 1772-1781).

stopTalk: version >= 7, GID_DIG/GID_CMI, HE and FM-Towns branches do not apply. MI1 DOS takes the v<=6 path: talk-stop animation, then setTalkingActor(0xFF), then restoreCharsetBg (actor.cpp:3576-3610).
getTalkingActor reads _V1TalkingActor only for GID_MANIAC v<=1 (actor.cpp:3344-3349).
rows.notes: Visibility effects, from the code path only and not checked at runtime. (1) If an invisible actor is put into the current room, _visible stays false until something calls showActor: o5_putActor via putActor (actor.cpp:1768-1770), or showActors on room entry (room.cpp:247; actor.cpp:2243-2249). (2) If a visible actor is put into a different non-zero room, _visible stays true and _moving is left as it was. walkActors and processActors skip actors not in the current room (actor.cpp:475-480, 2323-2328), so the actor is not drawn and its walk freezes. o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_ACTOR tests _moving without a room check (script_v5.cpp:3281-3286), so a wait on that actor would not end until something stops its walk; for example, hideActor stops it when the actor is later put in room 0 (actor.cpp:2178-2181). (3) Edge case while _currentRoom is 0: putActor treats room 0 as the current room, so a visible actor gets the stop-walk and adjustActorPos path instead of hideActor, and showActor returns early in room 0 (actor.cpp:1753-1759, 2199-2200). An invalid actor number is a fatal error through derefActor (script_v5.cpp:2165; actor.cpp:2286-2291). The room byte is not validated.

writes.detail: _cursor.state = 1. While state > 0: the mouse cursor is shown, Enter and Tab act as left and right clicks, and the verb hover highlight follows the mouse each frame (handleMouseOver and redrawVerbs only look up the verb under the mouse when state > 0).
verbMouseOver(0): the currently highlighted verb is redrawn unhighlighted and _verbMouseOver = 0, unless that verb is an image verb, in which case _verbMouseOver is left unchanged.
VAR_CURSORSTATE = _cursor.state and VAR_USERPUT = _userPut. These are re-synced after every subop because version >= 4.

game_specific: verbMouseOver returns early for version <= 2 without verbs and for GID_FT. Neither applies to MI1 (verbs.cpp:990-994).
rows.notes: SO_CURSOR_ON, case 1. Boot value is _cursor.state = 0 on DOS (scumm.cpp:2187). The cursor state on its own does not gate scripts; _userPut does (see UserputOn). It can be tested only through VAR_CURSORSTATE, which is a one-way mirror: no engine path copies the variable back into _cursor.state.

writes.detail: _cursor.state = 0, or 1 for GID_MONKEY on Macintosh. The mouse cursor is hidden, Enter and Tab no longer act as clicks (they reach the input script as plain keys), and the verb hover highlight stops following the mouse.
verbMouseOver(0): the verb highlight is cleared, unless the highlighted verb is an image verb.
VAR_CURSORSTATE and VAR_USERPUT are re-synced.

game_specific: GID_MONKEY on kPlatformMacintosh keeps _cursor.state = 1, so the cursor is never hidden. DOS is unaffected (script_v5.cpp:863).
rows.notes: SO_CURSOR_OFF, case 2. Mouse clicks still reach checkExecVerbs while _userPut > 0 (verbs.cpp:590). For input, only the Enter and Tab click substitutes depend on the cursor state; the other effects are the hidden cursor and the frozen verb hover highlight.

writes.detail: _userPut = 1. While _userPut > 0, checkExecVerbs turns player clicks and keys into runInputScript calls, which start VAR_VERB_SCRIPT.
VAR_USERPUT = 1, and VAR_CURSORSTATE is re-synced.

rows.notes: SO_USERPUT_ON, case 3. Central to causes: _userPut > 0 is the engine gate between player input and the verb or input script, checked in checkExecVerbs right after runAllScripts each frame (scumm.cpp:3231-3232; verbs.cpp:590). Boot value is _userPut = 0 (scumm.cpp:2188); a savegame restores it (saveload.cpp:1499). VAR_USERPUT is a one-way mirror: no engine path copies it back, so a script writing VAR_USERPUT directly does not change the gate. The Esc cutscene key is handled in processKeyboard and is not gated by _userPut (input.cpp:1422-1428).

writes.detail: _userPut = 0. checkExecVerbs then returns immediately, so clicks and keys do not start the verb or input script.
VAR_USERPUT = 0, and VAR_CURSORSTATE is re-synced.

rows.notes: SO_USERPUT_OFF, case 4. Input that arrives while _userPut <= 0 is dropped for that frame, not queued: processInput rebuilds _mouseAndKeyboardStat and clears the clicked flags every frame (input.cpp:439, 530-531), and checkExecVerbs returns before using it (verbs.cpp:590-591).

writes.detail: _cursor.state++, a counter. The cursor is shown, Enter and Tab act as clicks, and the verb hover highlight follows the mouse, while the counter is > 0.
verbMouseOver(0): the verb highlight is cleared, unless the highlighted verb is an image verb.
VAR_CURSORSTATE = the new counter, and VAR_USERPUT is re-synced.

rows.notes: SO_CURSOR_SOFT_ON, case 5. The result depends on the earlier counter value, so it is history dependent.

writes.detail: _cursor.state--, a counter that can go negative. When the counter is <= 0 the cursor is hidden, the Enter and Tab click substitutes are off, and the verb hover highlight stops following the mouse.
verbMouseOver(0): the verb highlight is cleared, unless the highlighted verb is an image verb.
VAR_CURSORSTATE = the new counter, and VAR_USERPUT is re-synced.

game_specific: GID_MONKEY on kPlatformMacintosh: a counter that reaches 0 is forced back to 1. DOS is unaffected (script_v5.cpp:878-879).
rows.notes: SO_CURSOR_SOFT_OFF, case 6.

writes.detail: _userPut++, a counter. Player input reaches the verb script only while _userPut > 0.
VAR_USERPUT = the new counter, and VAR_CURSORSTATE is re-synced.

rows.notes: SO_USERPUT_SOFT_ON, case 7. Nested enable and disable: input returns only when every soft-off has been matched by a soft-on, or a hard UserputOn resets the counter to 1.

writes.detail: _userPut--, a counter that can go negative. checkExecVerbs ignores input while _userPut <= 0.
VAR_USERPUT = the new counter, and VAR_CURSORSTATE is re-synced.

rows.notes: SO_USERPUT_SOFT_OFF, case 8.

writes.detail: _cursorImages[index] = the bitmap of one charset glyph (cursor shape), drawn with charset 1 for v>=4 (setCurID(1), not restored). It returns early if a Mac cursor file is loaded.
VAR_CURSORSTATE and VAR_USERPUT are re-synced.

reads: cursor index and glyph (var or immediate byte)
game_specific: assert(_game.id == GID_LOOM): this subop is supported only for Loom. The Mac-cursor-file early return comes before the assert, so on GID_MONKEY DOS (no Mac cursor file) the assert fails and aborts (cursor.cpp:874-879).
PC-Engine Loom uses a hard-coded cursor for index 1 (cursor.cpp:888-895). version 3 uses charset 0, v>=4 uses charset 1 (cursor.cpp:897-901).
rows.notes: SO_CURSOR_IMAGE, case 10. Not used by MI1.

writes.detail: _cursorHotspots[index*2] = x and [index*2+1] = y.
VAR_CURSORSTATE and VAR_USERPUT are re-synced.

reads: index, x, y (var or immediate bytes)
game_specific: assert(_game.id == GID_LOOM): Loom only, with no early return. On GID_MONKEY the assert would abort (cursor.cpp:935).
rows.notes: SO_CURSOR_HOTSPOT, case 11. Not used by MI1.

writes.detail: _currentCursor = i for i in 0..3, otherwise a fatal error(). This selects which built-in cursor image and hotspot setBuiltinCursor uses.
VAR_CURSORSTATE and VAR_USERPUT are re-synced.

rows.notes: SO_CURSOR_SET, case 12. descumm calls it InitCursor. Not used by MI1.

writes.detail: Loads the charset resource if it is not already loaded.
_string[0]._default.charset and _string[1]._default.charset = charsetno. This sets the default font for later talk, print and verb text.
_charsetColorMap = a copy of _charsetData[charsetno], the 16 text colours.
VAR_CURSORSTATE and VAR_USERPUT are re-synced.

game_specific: initCharset uses a different 'is loaded' test for GID_FT. Not MI1 (string.cpp:2013-2019).
rows.notes: SO_CHARSET_SET, case 13. Rendering state only; no opcode reads the selected charset directly. The only indirect read is o5_getStringWidth, which measures with the current charset ID; that ID is set from _string[].charset when text is next drawn (script_v5.cpp:1138-1150; string.cpp:1102, 1377). MI1 does not use o5_getStringWidth. The charset changes glyph widths and so text wrapping, but I found no path from it into message duration, which is driven by VAR_CHARINC per character. Not fully traced.

writes.detail: v>=4: the word list (up to NUM_SCRIPT_LOCAL items, the rest zeroed) is read. _charsetColorMap[0..15] and _charsetData[_string[1]._default.charset][0..15] = table[i], so unlisted entries become 0.
VAR_CURSORSTATE and VAR_USERPUT are re-synced.

game_specific: version 3: two byte arguments are read and ignored (script_v5.cpp:910-915).
GID_MONKEY on kPlatformFMTowns without kEnhVisualChanges: the table is read with stride 2, which reproduces an original interpreter bug. DOS uses stride 1 (script_v5.cpp:925).
rows.notes: Case 14, marked 'unk' in the source; descumm prints CursorCommand([...]) for v>=4. MI1 uses it once. Cosmetic text colours only. Opcode values with no case (for example 9 or 15+) fall to default, which does nothing except re-sync VAR_CURSORSTATE and VAR_USERPUT (script_v5.cpp:930-937).

writes.detail: [queue branch, verb != 0xFE] Pushes {verb, objectA, objectB, preposition = (objectB != 0), freezeCount = 0} onto the sentence queue _sentence[]. The queue is LIFO with at most NUM_SENTENCE = 6 entries; overflow fails an assert.
[STOP branch, verb == 0xFE] _sentenceNum = 0: all queued sentences are discarded.

[STOP branch] Every live instance of the script named by VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT is killed. If the opcode runs inside the sentence script itself, it kills its own caller, which does not continue. In v5, killing one that holds an active override is a fatal error().

[STOP branch] clearClickedStatus: _keyPressed is reset, _mouseAndKeyboardStat = 0, and the clicked flags of both mouse buttons and the wheel flag are cleared. When the opcode runs inside runAllScripts (after processInput, before checkExecVerbs), input taken this frame never reaches the verb script. When it runs from the verb script (nested in checkExecVerbs via runInputScript) or from the sentence script, this frame's input was already consumed, and processInput rebuilds the state next frame anyway.

reads: verb (var or immediate byte), objectA and objectB (vars or immediate words)

starts.what: [queue branch, indirect] At the end of the same frame, after runAllScripts and checkExecVerbs, checkAndRunSentenceScript pops the newest entry. It runs VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT nested (not freeze-resistant, not recursive) with Local[0] = verb, Local[1] = objectA, Local[2] = objectB. This happens only if no live, unfrozen instance of that script exists and the top entry's freezeCount is 0.
[STOP branch] Stops the script in VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT.

blocks.until: The opcode returns at once. The sentence runs later, in the same frame at the earliest. A script that must wait for it uses o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_SENTENCE.

cost_knobs.effect: A queued sentence waits while any live, unfrozen instance of VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT exists, so queued sentences run one after another, each after the previous run finishes.
checkAndRunSentenceScript is called once per scummLoop and pops at most one entry, so N queued sentences take at least N frames even when each sentence script finishes within its frame.

cost_knobs.knob: freezeScripts / unfreezeScripts (o5_freezeScripts, for example from a cutscene-start script)
cost_knobs.effect: freezeScripts increments the freezeCount of every queue entry. A frozen top entry is not consumed until unfreezeScripts decrements it to 0. A frozen sentence-script instance does not hold the queue back.

game_specific: GID_MONKEY, GID_MONKEY_EGA and GID_MONKEY_VGA with kEnhMinorBugFixes: when the popped sentence is a Give of one specific note object, still owned by the room, to one specific actor, it is consumed and a Pick-up sentence for that object is queued instead. This does fire for GID_MONKEY DOS CD when enhancements are on (script.cpp:1199-1200, 1275-1295).
version < 7: a popped sentence that has a preposition and objectB == objectA is dropped without running any script. This applies to MI1 (script.cpp:1202-1204).
version >= 7 drops A == B and exact repeats at push time. Not MI1 (script.cpp:1148-1162).
GID_FT sentence-script substitution and the v<=2 variable-based path do not apply to MI1 (script.cpp:1180-1181, 1206-1210, 1217-1242).
rows.notes: This is one function with two branches, not a sub-op byte. verb 0xFE is descumm's doSentence(STOP); a text count gives 27 of the 122 MI1 lines. The queue is LIFO: _sentenceNum-- takes the most recently pushed entry (script.cpp:1196). If VAR_SENTENCE_SCRIPT is 0, the popped entry is discarded and nothing runs (script.cpp:1245). The sentence script is started with runScript non-recursive, so a frozen older instance of it is killed first (script.cpp:65-66). The queue cannot be tested by any opcode; o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_SENTENCE can only block on it. The sentence script's running state is testable with o5_isScriptRunning. clearClickedStatus also calls a local speedrun hook (input.cpp:379); this is a local patch, not upstream ScummVM.

writes.detail: Current slot: delay = the value of the given variable (always a variable, never immediate), status = ssPaused. Then breakHere saves the script pointer and ends this script's turn (_currentScript = 0xFF).

blocks.until: Resumes on the first frame where the slot's delay goes below 0. Each frame, decreaseScriptDelay runs before runAllScripts and subtracts delta, where delta = VAR_TIMER_NEXT raised to at least 1 and capped at 15 for this countdown. A delay d therefore resumes after floor(d/delta)+1 frames. d <= 0 resumes on the next frame, like breakHere.

cost_knobs.effect: Jiffies consumed per frame. A larger value means fewer frames for the same delay. Wall time per frame is delta*4 quarter-frames of the timer.
Script delays count down at most 15 jiffies per frame, even when VAR_TIMER_NEXT is larger.

cost_knobs.knob: freezeScripts (in v5 only through o5_freezeScripts, which a cutscene-start script may call; beginCutscene itself does not freeze) vs freezeResistant
cost_knobs.effect: A frozen paused slot has status ssPaused|0x80, and decreaseScriptDelay only counts down status == ssPaused, so the delay stops counting while the slot is frozen. This does not apply to freeze-resistant scripts unless the freeze flag is >= 0x80.

cost_knobs.knob: Esc, or both mouse buttons at once (v4+) / cutscene override
cost_knobs.effect: abortCutscene sets the override-owning slot's status to ssRunning, its freezeCount to 0, and jumps it to its override point, which cancels a pending delay in that one script. It is enabled only while VAR_CUTSCENEEXIT_KEY != 0, and it sets VAR_OVERRIDE = 1.
The delay does not expire while TTS is speaking; it keeps counting down.
Shortens or removes the wall-clock wait per frame. The number of frames is unchanged.
Zeroes the wall-clock wait per frame. Frame count is unchanged.

game_specific: decreaseScriptDelay has a GID_INDY3 Macintosh credits hook (script.cpp:1527-1540).
o5_breakHere has a GID_LOOM PC-Engine injected delay (script_v5.cpp:825-828).
Main-loop delta adjustments for v0, GID_MANIAC v1, the INDY3/LOOM/ZAK name-entry rooms, v8, and FM-Towns smooth scrolling. None applies to GID_MONKEY DOS CD (scumm.cpp:2823-2881).
rows.notes: The unit is jiffies (1/60 s), consumed at VAR_TIMER_NEXT jiffies per frame. Unlike o5_delay, which takes a 24-bit immediate (script_v5.cpp:972-980), the count comes from a variable. The pause cannot be read back: o5_isScriptRunning reports paused slots as running, because it only checks status != ssDead (script.cpp:1557-1563). No frames run while the engine is paused (scumm.cpp:2892).

writes.detail: N consecutive variables, starting at the result variable, get the listed constants. Values are unsigned bytes, or signed words when opcode bit 0x80 is set. _resultVarNumber++ steps within the same space: global vars, or locals when the result is a 0x4000 local.
If the result variable is a bit variable (0x8000), consecutive bit variables are written: non-zero sets the bit, 0 clears it.

writeVar side effects on special engine variables. Writing VAR_NOSUBTITLES sets the ScummVM 'subtitles' setting (the value is asserted to be 0 or 1). Writing VAR_CHARINC calls setTalkSpeed(9-value) for values 0..9; in room 0, when the user has a target-specific talkspeed, the user value replaces the script's.

reads: result position (an indexed 0x2000 result reads an index var)
count byte and constant list from the script

cost_knobs.knob: Range that covers VAR_CHARINC or VAR_TIMER_NEXT
cost_knobs.effect: Same as any write to these variables: it changes the per-character message time (talk speed) or the jiffies per frame.

game_specific: writeVar has GID_SAMNMAX and GID_LOOM VAR_TIMER_NEXT tweaks and HE-only subtitle guards. None applies to MI1 (script.cpp:721-722, 728-729, 766-791).
rows.notes: An indexed (0x2000) result is resolved once in getResultPos (script_v5.cpp:383-396). A count byte of 0 is not guarded: do { } while (--a) on an int would not stop after 0, and would keep writing until a range assert fires (script_v5.cpp:2758-2766). MI1 does not use count 0. MI1 uses the byte (0x26) and word (0xA6) forms on globals, locals and bit variables; every MI1 global range starts above the engine-reserved variables, so no MI1 setVarRange reaches a writeVar side effect (checked against data/scripts-dos-cd).

writes.detail: result var = result var & operand. The operand is an immediate word or a var. The target may be a global, a local (0x4000) or a bit variable (0x8000).
The same writeVar side effects as any var write: VAR_NOSUBTITLES goes to the subtitles setting, VAR_CHARINC goes to talk speed.

reads: var (the target's current value; readVar of VAR_NOSUBTITLES returns the negated subtitles setting, script.cpp:592-594)
game_specific: readVar has GID_MONKEY2 guards (a var remap when copy protection is off; the Mac machine speed). Not MI1 (script.cpp:583-587, 599-601).

writes.detail: Sound::stopAllSounds. A playing CD audio track stops (_currentCDSound = 0, CD stopped, CD timer removed; only if a CD track is current). The pending start queue (_soundQueue: sounds started but not yet triggered) is cleared and Sound::_lastSound = 0. The music engine stops all its sounds; for MI1 DOS CD that is iMuse driving an AdLib MIDI driver, not Player_AD. Every mixer channel stops. The queued iMuse commands (_midiQueue) are not cleared.

VAR_MUSIC_TIMER stops advancing. For GF_AUDIOTRACKS games, which include the MI1 CD release, the per-frame update copies _cdMusicTimer. stopAllCDSounds neither resets that counter nor keeps its timer, so the variable holds its last value. Under the local speedrun patch the timer is advanced from the engine's waits only while _cdTimerByTicks is set, which stopCDTimer clears, so the result is the same.

cost_knobs.knob: Scripts that wait on VAR_MUSIC_TIMER or on o5_isSoundRunning
cost_knobs.effect: After a stop, isSoundRunning returns 0 and VAR_MUSIC_TIMER no longer rises. A loop that waits for a sound to end exits at once, and a loop that waits for the timer to reach a value never exits. This is inferred from the code and not traced in MI1, which never uses this opcode.

game_specific: Ambience stop only when _enableAmbienceSounds is on, and that flag is set only for GF_DOUBLEFINE_PAK (Special Edition) builds of GID_MONKEY or GID_MONKEY2. It does not apply to DOS CD (sound.cpp:90-95, 978-979).
The mixer stopAll is skipped when iMuse Digital is active (v7+). Not MI1 (sound.cpp:991-993).

writes.detail: Destination var from getResultPos: a global, a local (0x4000) or a bit var (0x8000), optionally indexed with 0x2000. It is set to the final stack top by the epilogue setResult(pop()), which writeVar performs. This write happens on every Exprmode, whatever the sub-ops.

If the destination is VAR_CHARINC, writeVar also stores a user setting. When the value is 0..9, setTalkSpeed(9-value) writes ConfMan 'talkspeed' scaled to 0..255 as ((9-value)*255+4)/9. In room 0 (_currentRoom == 0), if the target has its own talkspeed key, the script's value is replaced by 9-getTalkSpeed(), so the stored var then comes from the user's config, not the script.

If the destination is VAR_NOSUBTITLES (var 60 in v5), the write is mirrored to the subtitles config as !value and asserts that value is 0 or 1. readVar of that var returns !subtitles from the config, for any reader.

reads: var (any global, local or bit var as operand, engine VAR_ values included, e.g. VAR_CAMERA_POS_X)
var used as index for 0x2000-indexed operands or destination

writes.detail: Var 0 (ScummVM VAR_KEYPRESS, descumm VAR_RESULT) is written by a nested o5_getRandomNr. The nested opcode writes whatever result var its own bytecode names (its own getResultPos), but the engine then pushes the raw _scummVars[0] regardless, so the nested value reaches the expression only when the nested opcode targets var 0. All 191 nested uses in MI1 do (descumm prints <VAR_RESULT = ...>). Var 0 keeps the value after the expression ends.

Var 0 is written the same way by nested getter opcodes (getActorX, getActorY, getActorElevation, getActorWidth, getActorFacing, getDist, getInventoryCount in MI1), each through its own getResultPos/setResult.
Destination var via the epilogue setResult(pop()). It carries the nested random number when the nested opcode is getRandomNr.
Destination var via the epilogue. It carries engine-computed values (actor position, distance, inventory count, etc.) when the nested opcode is a getter.

In principle this case inherits all writes, starts and blocking of whatever is nested, and ScummVM does not special-case a blocking nested opcode. In MI1 only getters are nested, in 191 Exprmode lines: getRandomNr 141, getActorX 33, getActorY 19, getActorElevation 2, getInventoryCount 1, getDist 1, getActorWidth 1, getActorFacing 1. used_in_mi1 comes from these script counts; prefill has no per-case data. With keep-text off, stopTalk first switches the previous talking actor to its _talkStopFrame (if that actor is in the room and _useTalkAnims is set). Then the ego's costume switches to _talkStartFrame, skipped if _frame already equals it, and again at the start of each wait() chunk. stopTalk later switches it to _talkStopFrame. writes.detail: Draws the text: overhead above the ego, or at the Pos/Center position. Before drawing it erases the previous message (restoreCharsetBg) unless keep-text is on.

Text slot 0 (VAR_EGO values 252-254 would pick slots 3/2/1) is reset from its defaults by loadDefault. The Pos/Color/Clipped/Center/Left/Overhead sub-ops then set xpos/ypos, color, right clip, center and overhead. Order matters: Pos and Center clear overhead, and Overhead sets it. With a Text sub-op, SO_TEXTSTRING returns before saveDefault, so the settings last for that line only. Without a Text sub-op, nothing is printed and saveDefault stores the settings as slot 0's defaults, which every later slot-0 message (printEgo, and o5_print for an actor or 255) starts from. MI1 uses this layout-only form in 10 lines (e.g. Pos+Center+Color). The slot color is not used for the ego's own speech: actorTalk takes _charsetColor from the actor's talk color whenever the talking actor is below 0x80. It only shows up through the defaults, in later narrator (255) messages.

Message engine state. _charsetBuffer is always refilled from the text, with embedded getInt/getVerb/getName/getString codes expanded, even when the ego is in another room and nothing else happens (the refill comes before the room check). When the ego is in the room, the previous message is stopped first unless keep-text is on (stopTalkSound, _haveMsg=0, restore background, _keepText=false). Then _charsetBufPos=0, _talkDelay=0, _haveMsg=0xFF, _haveActorSpeechMsg=true and _useTalkAnims are set, and _charsetColor is set from the actor's talk color. displayDialog then sets _talkDelay, _keepText and _msgCount.

reads: VAR_EGO (cast to byte; picks text slot 0 unless it is 252-254)
Sub-op operands (literal or var via getVarOrDirectWord/Byte) and the inline text bytes
Text slot 0 defaults (set by earlier layout-only print/printEgo lines)
Vars, verb names, object/actor names and string resources referenced by embedded codes (getInt, getVerb, getName, getString)
Ego actor: room (isInCurrentRoom), position, elevation, scale, talk color, charset, talk start/stop frames, current _frame
Previous message state (_keepText, current talking actor, _useTalkAnims)
Camera position (text waits while the camera scrolls)

blocks.until: Never blocks. The opcode returns and the engine keeps the message going in later frames. A script that wants to wait uses o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_MESSAGE (VAR_HAVE_MSG) itself. In MI1, 242 printEgo lines are directly followed by WaitForMessage.

cost_knobs.effect: Adds VAR_CHARINC jiffies per character of each chunk. The characters count even when subtitles hide the text. The value comes from the talkspeed config at startup and from the +/- keys. A script write is replaced by the configured talkspeed only while _currentRoom == 0 and the target has a talkspeed key. Otherwise the write is stored, and also saved to the config when it is 0-9.

cost_knobs.knob: Fixed base delay (VAR_DEFAULT_TALK_DELAY unmapped in v5)
cost_knobs.effect: Each chunk starts with 60 jiffies, because VAR_DEFAULT_TALK_DELAY stays 0xFF in v5 (setupScummVars never maps it).
Split the line into chunks. Each chunk gets its own 60 + VAR_CHARINC*chars delay, and the message only ends after the last chunk.
Sets _haveMsg=0 right after drawing, so VAR_HAVE_MSG goes to 0 without waiting for the delay.
Sets _talkDelay=0, so the current chunk ends at that frame's displayDialog. The key works unless the script sets VAR_TALKSTOP_KEY to 0.
Each frame lowers _talkDelay by min(VAR_TIMER_NEXT,15) jiffies, so VAR_TIMER_NEXT sets how many frames one chunk lasts.
In v4-6, displayDialog does nothing while the camera is moving, so the text and its countdown start late.

actorTalk returns before stopTalk and before setting VAR_HAVE_MSG. Nothing is shown and any previous message keeps running. A following WaitForMessage passes at once only if no earlier message is still active.
While TTS is still speaking, displayDialog keeps the current chunk on screen.

game_specific: injectMISESpeech only acts when Sound::shouldInjectMISEAudio() is true (MI1 Special Edition remastered audio). It has no effect on the DOS CD release (script_v5.cpp:2037-2056; string.cpp:1207-1217).

SO_COLOR: an Indy3 Macintosh color hack (script_v5.cpp:3477-3478). A GID_MONKEY guard (not Ultimate Talkie, not SegaCD/FM-Towns/Mac, one specific room+script+color, kEnhVisualChanges) swaps one sign's text color for the closest palette green. It applies to MI1 DOS CD when enhancements are on (script_v5.cpp:3494-3504). For printEgo it only changes the slot color, which actor speech does not use (actor.cpp:3514-3526).
SO_LEFT sets the height instead when _game.version == 3 (script_v5.cpp:3523-3530).

SO_ERASE always calls error(), and so does SO_SAY_VOICE except for Loom v4. Any other sub-op code (5, 9-14) hits the default error() (script_v5.cpp:3511-3517; script_v5.cpp:3534-3566; script_v5.cpp:3571-3572).

decodeParseStringTextString has text fixes for Loom, Indy3 FM-Towns, Indy4 and MI1 EGA. The GID_MONKEY CD color fixes for the ghost priest and navigator lines need _actorToPrintStrFor == 255, so printEgo does not hit them unless VAR_EGO is 255. The GID_MONKEY room+script cannibal patch only swaps strings that begin with '/LH.xxx/' (Ultimate Talkie) and otherwise prints normally (script_v5.cpp:3579-3708; script_v5.cpp:3733-3761).
_game.version <= 3 copies position and color into the slot defaults (script_v5.cpp:3724-3729).
printString has GID_MONKEY2 and GID_SAMNMAX workarounds only (string.cpp:70-104).

actorTalk/displayDialog: Loom empty-string check, NES/Apple2GS colors, HE paths, the v4-6 camera wait, v<=5 overhead Y from VAR_V5_TALK_STRING_Y, v>3 automatic line breaks, SegaCD wrapping, and RTL handling for GID_MONKEY/GID_MONKEY2 (actor.cpp:3466-3538; string.cpp:1045-1093; string.cpp:1155-1186).
handleNextCharsetCode has a GID_SAMNMAX timing table for wait codes (string.cpp:289-480).
rows.notes: One row rather than one per sub-op. decodeParseString's sub-ops (Pos=SO_AT, Color, Clipped, Center, Left, Overhead, Text) all set up the same single message rather than choosing different actions, and prefill lists no subops. The only split that matters is whether a Text sub-op is present (see the string write): with Text, a message is shown; without it (layout-only), slot-0 defaults are stored and nothing is shown. MI1 has 879 lines: 869 with Text and 10 layout-only. Pos is in 13 lines, Center in 6, Color in 3, Overhead in 1. wait() appears 189 times across 135 lines; newline() is in 4 lines, getVerb() in 3, getInt() in 1, getName() in 1. The first chunk is drawn inside the opcode (actorTalk -> displayDialog), so the same script sees VAR_HAVE_MSG=0xFF straight away. _talkDelay drops at the start of each frame (scumm.cpp:3134). In the frame where it reaches 0, displayDialog runs after scripts and calls stopTalk, and scripts read VAR_HAVE_MSG=0 from the next frame on, because the copy runs before runAllScripts. Each chunk lasts 60 + VAR_CHARINC*chars jiffies. In v5, runActorTalkScript never starts a script: _talkScript is only set by v6/v8 actorOps (script_v6.cpp:2370, script_v8.cpp:905), so it calls startAnimActor (actor.cpp:3549-3561). Code 10 (digital talkie) would call Sound::talkSound (string.cpp:496-508). MI1 DOS CD is marked GUIO_NOSPEECH (detection_tables.h:199), so it is expected to be unused, but this was not checked against the data. 239 printEgo lines are followed by stopObjectCode, and the message keeps running after the script ends.

writes.detail: _pos is set to the script's (x,y). If the actor is in the current room and does not ignore boxes, adjustActorPos moves it into the nearest walk box (search thresholds 30/80/0). An actor in another room keeps the raw coordinates until showActor runs at the next startScene. This is a teleport. o5_actorFromPos only sees the new spot after the actor is redrawn, because it tests _top/_bottom and the gfx usage bits.

writes.detail: Walk box and scale: setBox stores the chosen box in _walkbox (kInvalidBox = 0 for MI1 when none is found). setupActorScale recomputes _scalex/_scaley from the box scale at the new position. For an actor that ignores boxes, adjustXYToBeInBox returns kInvalidBox, so _walkbox becomes 0 and setupActorScale returns early, keeping the old scale. This only happens when the actor is in the current room, with adjustActorPos called directly or through showActor.

writes.detail: Motion. Visible actor already in the current room: a walk in progress stops (_moving=0, walk destination cleared, stand frame started). If the new box has any of flags&7 set, adjustActorPos then calls turnToDirection(_facing), so _moving = MF_TURN (4) when the opcode returns (unless _ignoreTurns). For the rest of that frame o5_getActorMoving reads 4 and o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_ACTOR yields. walkActor runs after scripts each frame. On its first pass it clears _moving if the remapped direction equals _facing; otherwise it turns the actor and clears _moving on a later pass. MF_TURN therefore lasts 1-2 frames, or more when interpolated. Hidden actor being shown: showActor calls stopActorMoving after adjustActorPos, so MF_TURN is cleared at once and no turn happens.

writes.detail: When a visible actor already in the current room lands in a box with flags&7, the next walkActor pass computes the target with remapDirection. Box flags 1-6 force a fixed direction (90/270/0/180, or a left/right or up/down choice). _extraBoxFlags and X/Y-flip boxes can also change it. If the result differs from _facing, setDirection sets _facing and switches the costume to that direction. Nothing turns when the actor ignores boxes (remapDirection skips the box checks in v5, and _walkbox is invalid) or ignores turns.

writes.detail: Visibility and animation: a hidden actor in the current room is shown (showActor: costume loaded, init frame started if the costume needs init, _visible=true, _needRedraw=true). A visible actor whose room is not the current room is hidden. startAnimActor resets _cost.animCounter. The costume sound counters are cleared.

game_specific: GID_MONKEY with one specific close-up room, one specific actor and kEnhVisualChanges: two specific coordinate pairs are rewritten to the VGA-floppy values (alignment of the cigar smoke in the Captain Smirk close-up). Applies to MI1 DOS CD when enhancements are on, and changes what getActorX/Y return for that actor (script_v5.cpp:2111-2118).
GID_ZAK FM-Towns: one specific putActor is skipped (script_v5.cpp:2125-2127).

Actor::putActor: GID_SAMNMAX adds 1 to x in one case (actor.cpp:1738-1739); heversion>=62 sets a background reset (actor.cpp:1746-1747); HE71 queues aux erase (actor.cpp:1762-1765); version 0 resets walk fields (actor.cpp:1773-1778); GID_MANIAC v<=1 faces the camera (actor.cpp:1781-1782).

adjustXYToBeInBox: version<=4 falls back to the last valid XY; GF_SMALL_HEADER changes the first valid box and kInvalidBox; version>=7 starts bestDist larger (actor.cpp:1990; actor.cpp:2012-2015; actor.cpp:2032; scumm.cpp:2085).

turnToDirection: v0 sets direction immediately, v<=2 ORs MF_TURN, later versions assign MF_TURN (actor.cpp:1680-1685). remapDirection: v>=7 and v0 branches differ (actor.cpp:1456-1500). v5 games use the plain Actor class (scumm.cpp:2088-2100).
showActor: separate branches for version 0 and version <=2 (actor.cpp:2205-2230).
rows.notes: Room does not change: putActor(x,y) passes the actor's own _room (actor.h:221-223). stopActorMoving would stop _walkScript, but in v5 that is always 0 because only v6/v8 actorOps set it (actor.cpp:182, 231; script_v6.cpp:2348; script_v8.cpp:902), so no script stops. The stopTalk branch (actor.cpp:1731-1733) needs a visible actor whose own room differs from the current room, which o5_putActor can hit only in that unusual state. If the camera follows this actor, moveCamera reacts later in the same frame, after scripts (scumm.cpp:3285; camera.cpp:119-123). There are no cost knobs: the move is instant. It ends a walk in progress. A following o5_wait SO_WAIT_FOR_ACTOR returns at once, except when an already visible in-room actor lands in a box with flags&7; then the wait yields 1-2 frames while MF_TURN is cleared and the facing may change. It is the instant alternative to walking. derefActor stops with a fatal error on an invalid actor id (actor.cpp:2286-2291).

writes.detail: The result variable (global, bit or local; index taken from getResultPos) receives _rnd.getRandomNumber(max), a value in [0, max] inclusive.
The shared engine RNG state moves forward one step (scrambleSeed). Dissolve room transitions draw from the same stream, so the order of calls changes later results.

reads: Index var when the result variable is indexed

cost_knobs.knob: RNG seed (config key random_seed, or event-recorder seed)
cost_knobs.effect: Costs no time, but fixes the random sequence. MI1 often feeds these values into delays and branches. Without the key, the seed comes from wall-clock time and millis.

game_specific: Nothing in the opcode body. The shared var paths have guards: readVar remaps a GID_MONKEY2 var and returns 2 for the MI2 Mac machine speed. In v5, VAR_NOSUBTITLES (var 60) is mapped, so writing it sets the subtitles config and reading it returns the config value. Writes to VAR_CHARINC change the talk speed. SAMNMAX/Loom VAR_TIMER_NEXT tweaks also exist (script.cpp:582-600; script.cpp:716-754; script.cpp:756-790; vars.cpp:173-175).
rows.notes: max is read with getVarOrDirectByte: a literal 0-255, or any var value. A negative var value becomes a huge uint; max==UINT_MAX returns the raw product (common/random.cpp:63-66). Prefill's 194 MI1 lines are standalone opcode lines: 148 Var, 27 Local and 19 VAR_RESULT (e.g. 'VAR_RESULT = getRandomNr(1);'). Prefill does not count another 137 lines (141 calls) where getRandomNr runs nested inside o5_expression: expression case 6 executes the embedded opcode and pushes var 0 (script_v5.cpp:1182-1185). That makes 331 lines in all. Local results can only be read back by the same script slot. This tree's speedrun bridge can set the RNG state through set_rng (engines/scumm/speedrun/speedrun_control.cpp:327-336). That is a project addition, not upstream ScummVM.

writes.detail: Stops sound id N everywhere it can play. If N is the current CD-track sound, the CD audio and CD timer stop and _currentCDSound is set to 0. The mixer stops digital SFX with id N, iMUSE clears the player for N, and pending starts of N in _soundQueue are zeroed so processSoundQueues skips them.

writes.detail: With GF_AUDIOTRACKS (MI1 DOS CD), VAR_MUSIC_TIMER is copied from the CD music timer every frame. Stopping the current CD sound removes the timer proc, so VAR_MUSIC_TIMER stops rising and keeps its last value; it is not reset.

reads: Sound id operand (literal byte or var)
Current CD sound, mixer handles, iMUSE players, sound queue
VAR_ROOM, VAR_NEW_ROOM, current script slot, kEnhAudioChanges (MI1 workaround guard)
game_specific: GID_MONKEY with GF_AUDIOTRACKS (true for the DOS CD release, detection_tables.h:199), while the room-exit script (kScriptNumEXCD) moves between two specific rooms, for one specific sound, with kEnhAudioChanges: the stop is skipped so the outdoor ambience keeps playing in the Captain Smirk close-up. Applies to MI1 DOS CD when enhancements are on (script_v5.cpp:2851-2853; script.h:120-121).
GID_MANIAC NES: also clears a music-status script var in one case (script_v5.cpp:2859-2861).
Sound::stopSound: mixer stopID only when version<7; SE ambience stopped when _enableAmbienceSounds (sound.cpp:953-958).
SoundCD::stopCDTimer does nothing when replacement audio tracks are used (Loom) (soundcd.cpp:131-132).
For MI1 DOS CD the music engine is iMUSE; Player_AD is only for Loom/Indy3 (scumm.cpp:2524; scumm.cpp:2573-2580). The read-back side ignores fade-outs only for GID_MONKEY2 (imuse/imuse.cpp:738-749).
rows.notes: A stop only touches the CD when N is the current CD sound (soundcd.cpp:61). The iMUSE command queue (_midiQueue) is not purged. iMUSE Player::clear fires ImFireAllTriggers (imuse/imuse_player.cpp:158; imuse/imuse.cpp:1342-1355), but triggers can only be set by Sam&Max (imuse/imuse.cpp:850-864), so this starts nothing in MI1. No cost knobs: the stop itself is instant. It makes a script loop that polls o5_isSoundRunning, or one waiting on VAR_MUSIC_TIMER, finish early or never. If a script waits for VAR_MUSIC_TIMER to pass a value after the CD track was stopped, it may never finish, because the timer stays frozen.

writes.detail: The result variable receives the actor's _walkbox. That is the last box set while walking (setBox when a leg enters the next box or ends), by adjustActorPos (putActor/showActor and other placement), or kInvalidBox when startWalkActor or adjustActorPos runs for an actor that ignores boxes. For MI1, 0 means no box (kInvalidBox is 0 because MI1 does not have GF_SMALL_HEADER).

The value is not refreshed for actors outside the current room: it stays whatever was last set. v5 uses the plain Actor class, so the walking writers are Actor::actorWalkStep (actor.cpp:648) and Actor::walkActor (actor.cpp:958, 980, 987, 1010). The setBox calls at actor.cpp:723 and 1249-1391 belong to Actor_v3/v2/v0. MI1 has 38 lines: 26 VAR_RESULT, 9 Local, 3 Var.

reads: Current value of the result variable

There is no overflow check. Writing to a bit var keeps only whether the result is non-zero (script.cpp:822-829). MI1 has 11 lines (7 Local, 4 Var), for example Var[x] *= 10.

game_specific: Only opcode 0xA7 maps to it (script_v5.cpp:250). The comment says the MI2 Amiga KIXX XL release uses 0xA7 as a dummy, yet the condition warns for MI2, which looks reversed. Either way it does nothing.

The VAR_ROOM_FLAG path from this subop is therefore practically unreachable. The same write mainly comes from room entry. startScene sets _roomResource and then calls ensureResourceLoaded for the new room (room.cpp:166-175), which reaches resource.cpp:643-644 when the room is not resident. That pass skips locked and in-use resources (resource.cpp:1123-1152; thresholds at scumm.cpp:1772-1788). Any getResourceAddress on the resource before then sets the counter back to 1 (resource.cpp:788), which cancels the mark. Freed resources are reloaded on demand (resource.cpp:777-780). Running scripts count as in use (resource.cpp:1041-1042).

The next getResourceAddress on the sound, for example when it is triggered (sound.cpp:201), sets the counter back to 1 (resource.cpp:788). If a sound is actually freed, isSoundRunning's residency check can return 0 for it (sound.cpp:875-876). That is the only indirect effect a script could see.

writes.detail: VAR_MUSIC_TIMER = 0 (v5 defines it)
VAR_LAST_SOUND = sound id
The sound id is appended to the sound queue. isSoundRunning reports 1 while it is queued, unless the id is the current CD sound, which is checked first.

At the end of the frame the queue is triggered:
- CD-track SOUN resources (type 2) start CD audio. Track, loops and start/end come from the resource. This also sets the current CD sound and resets the CD music timer. If the id is already the current CD sound and pollCD() == 1, the trigger is skipped: no restart and no timer reset.
- SBL resources play as mixer samples.
- Other resources go to iMuse.
isSoundRunning then reports pollCD for the CD sound, the mixer id for samples, or iMuse status.

rows.notes: On MI1 CD the VAR_MUSIC_TIMER = 0 write does not last. Scripts later in the same frame see 0, but scummLoop overwrites the variable from _cdMusicTimer before the next frame's scripts: scumm.cpp:3200 runs before runAllScripts at scumm.cpp:3231. The value restarts from 0 only if the trigger actually starts a CD track, because playCDTrack resets the timer (soundcd.cpp:150-152). If the same CD sound is still playing, triggerSound returns early (sound.cpp:324-325) and the CD timer is not reset. VAR_MUSIC_TIMER then jumps back to the running timer at the next updateMusicTimer. The trigger itself waits until scummLoop_handleSound, after scripts (scumm.cpp:3315). The queue is drained last-in first-out (sound.cpp:156-160). isSoundRunning checks _currentCDSound before the queue (sound.cpp:866-873), so re-queuing the current CD sound after its track ended reports 0 until it is triggered. With the fork's speedrun bridge the CD timer runs on game time, but pollCD still asks the AudioCDManager (soundcd.cpp:204-206). How that behaves headless was not traced. This opcode does not write VAR_SOUNDRESULT; only the MIDI queue does (sound.cpp:163-185).
